item.title: A convergent Lagrangian scheme for the Navier Stokes equations on the normed Wasserstein space
item.description: arXiv:2611.14662v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the differential structure on Wasserstein spaces of Schichl (arXiv:2508.15140) to the normed Wasserstein space $\mathbb{W}_1$ of finite signed measures, the natural setting for measure differential equations with source terms. We generalize the averaged flow dispersion and expectational flow operators to $\mathbb{W}_1$ and show that along divergence--free tangent vectors they act by measure--preserving flows, and further define source operators. As an application, we construct a purely Lagrangian splitting scheme for the incompressible Navier--Stokes equations on $\mathbb{R}^N$, inspired by the Averaged Flow Approximation Series (AFAS) in \cite{Schichl2025}. We recover, with explicit constants, the classical lifespan bound, a blow--up rate and the inviscid limit with rate $O(\eta^2)$, and a linearised scheme yields $L^{\infty}$, H\"older, $L^1$ and moment estimates for classical solutions.
item.dc:creator: Arthur Schichl

item.title: Damped wave equation with a dynamic boundary condition: sharp resolvent estimate
item.description: arXiv:2611.14751v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work investigates the stabilization of a wave equation with a localized damping and dynamic boundary conditions. This model traces back to the classical treatment of torsion and impact problems. Consider a second-order hyperbolic equation posed with a dynamic boundary condition on a smooth compact Riemannian manifold $(\M,g)$ with boundary, in which the damping acts either in the interior or on $\d \M$. Under the assumption that the damping is positive on an open subset of its domain of action, a resolvent estimate is established. A logarithmic decay rate is then deduced for the energy of strong solutions. We provide examples that establish the sharpness of the resolvent estimate.
item.dc:creator: R\'emi Buffe, Victor Hugo Gonzalez Martinez, J\'er\^ome Le Rousseau, Luc Robbiano

item.title: The higher order regularity problem for elliptic systems with data in Banach function spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.14787v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We characterize the well-posedness of the higher order regularity problem in the upper half-space with data in Sobolev Banach function spaces by proving its equivalence to natural weighted estimates for the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator. The generality of our framework allows for applications to Lebesgue spaces, rearrangement-invariant spaces such as Orlicz spaces, and variable exponent Lebesgue spaces, as well as their weighted counterparts, among others. This is established for the family of second-order, homogeneous, elliptic, constant complex coefficient systems in ${\mathbb{R}}^n$ that admit a distinguished coefficient tensor, a natural condition that always holds in the scalar case and for the Lam\'e system of elasticity.
item.dc:creator: Juan Jos\'e Mar\'in

item.title: Perimeter-Regularized Critical Shapes in the Class $\mathcal{O}_C$: Core-Normal Transfer and First-Order Return-Map Response
item.description: arXiv:2611.14859v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $C \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ be a compact strictly convex core and $\mathcal{O}_C$ denote the class of domains whose outer boundary is a global outward normal graph over $\partial C$ and whose inward boundary normals return to the interior of $C$. We study volume-constrained critical domains of the Dirichlet-perimeter functional: \[ \mathcal{E}_{\mu}(\Omega) = -\frac{1}{2}\int_{\Omega}|\nabla u_{\Omega}|^{2}\,\mathrm{d}x + \mu P(\Omega), \qquad -\Delta u_{\Omega} = f, \quad u_{\Omega}|_{\partial\Omega}=0, \] in the large-perimeter regime $\mu\to\infty$. We give an adapted Lyapunov--Schmidt construction near translated spheres to extract the first physical shape coefficient of scale $\mu^{-1}$. We then prove that $\mathcal{O}_C$ is open under small $C^1$ thickness perturbations and establish a quantitative coordinate-transfer theorem to a unique core-normal thickness. Finally, we prove that the forward return-map operator $d \mapsto F_d$ is Fr\'echet $C^1$ between H\"older spaces and provide its explicit derivative. This yields a shape-to-dynamics sensitivity theorem for $\mathcal{O}_C$: a perimeter-regularized PDE-constrained critical deformation produces an explicitly controlled first-order deformation of the return dynamics. A nonradial example confirms that the response coefficient is generically nonzero.
item.dc:creator: M. Barkatou, M. El Morsalani

item.title: Existence, relative Morse index and the number of positive multi-peak solutions to subcritical Hamiltonian systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.14899v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct positive multi-peak solutions of a singularly perturbed Hamiltonian elliptic system with a common uniformly positive potential $a$ and powers $p,q>1$ below the Sobolev critical hyperbola. The peaks concentrate at any prescribed set of $k$ distinct nondegenerate critical points $P_i$ of $a$. The Hessian of the action is strongly indefinite. A Schur complement gives exactly $kN$ eigenvalues near zero and their leading terms, which have order $\varepsilon^2$ and are determined by $D^2a(P_i)$. The solutions are nondegenerate. A scalar Schur reduction and localization of its inverse term give the relative Morse index $k+\sum_{i=1}^k\ind D^2a(P_i)$. Local Pohozaev identities give local uniqueness. A compactness argument then shows that, for $m$ prescribed nondegenerate critical points, the union of the fixed profile neighborhoods associated with their nonempty subsets contains exactly $2^m-1$ positive solutions. Using uniqueness of positive solutions of the limiting system up to translations, we obtain the same count in classes defined by nonvanishing in fixed balls and a scaled nonlinear mass bound that excludes an additional peak. We also give second-order expansions of the peak locations and rescaled profiles.
item.dc:creator: Qing Guo

item.title: Sharp asymptotics and stability for a two-power affine Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev inequality
item.description: arXiv:2611.14917v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the affine Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev inequality under the constraint $\frac{1}{2}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}(f^{q-\varepsilon}+f^{q+\varepsilon}) dx=1$ for $f\ge0$, where $q=\frac{2n}{n+\alpha}$, $n\ge2$, $0<\alpha<n$, and $0<\varepsilon<q-1$. We determine the second-order expansion of its sharp constant and the scale selected by all normalized radial extremals as $\varepsilon\rightarrow0^+$. For sufficiently small fixed $\varepsilon$, we prove stability estimates with power $2$ in $L^{q-\varepsilon}\cap L^{q+\varepsilon}$ for the Euclidean and affine energies. The power $2$ is sharp, and the sharp stability constants admit $O(\varepsilon^2)$ upper bounds as $\varepsilon\rightarrow0^+$. The proof combines identities for the two power integrals with Euclidean spectral estimates, affine compactness and a nonlinear directional expansion. No uniqueness or additional regularity of the radial extremals is assumed.
item.dc:creator: Zhenzhen Wei, Denghui Wu

item.title: Diffusion phenomena for evolution equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.14951v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the diffusion phenomenon for the abstract damped wave equation $u''+Bu'+Au=0$ on a Banach space and its possibly degenerate parabolic counterpart $Bv'+Av=0$. We assume that $B$ is bounded and the wave equation is well-posed, without requiring symmetry, injectivity, or commutativity of $A$ and $B$. Our aim is to identify initial data for which the parabolic solution is a genuine diffusive profile: $\|u(t)-v(t)\|=o(\|v(t)\|)$ as $t\to\infty$. Using Fourier analysis of resolvent expressions for the associated quadratic and linear operator pencils, we establish decay estimates for the difference of hyperbolic and parabolic solutions and their time derivatives. In particular, we characterize broad classes of initial data yielding the classical upper bounds of orders $t^{-1}$ and $t^{-2}$. We also prove lower bounds for both solutions, of the form $\|u(t)\|,\|v(t)\|\gtrsim r(t)$, for large sets of initial data and arbitrary prescribed functions $r(t)\to0$ that decay sufficiently slowly. Combining these results with high- and low-frequency resolvent estimates and a condition on the ranges of $A$ and $B$, we obtain genuine diffusive profiles. The analysis uses spectral properties of a sectorially holomorphic parabolic solution semigroup, which need not be strongly continuous. We apply the theory to damped wave equations on $L^2(\Omega)$ with the Dirichlet Laplacian and bounded nonnegative damping that may vanish on large sets. We establish criteria for the required resolvent and range conditions, treat the whole space and exterior domains, and construct diffusive initial data using Weyl sequences.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Kr\'ol, Yuri Latushkin, Yuri Tomilov

item.title: Remarks on the BKM criterion for both classical and variable Euler systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.14954v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish new results on BKM-type criteria for the incompressible Euler equations on $\mathbb{R}^3$ as well as the Euler equations with space-time variable coefficients in a bounded domain. Our first result shows that if a finite-energy solution to the Euler equations on $\mathbb{R}^3$ blows up at a time $T_\ast$, and $T_\ast$ is the first such time, then $\limsup_{t\to T_\ast^-}(T_\ast -t)^{1+2k/5}\|D^k\omega(t)\|_{L^\infty} = \infty$ for every $k \geq 1$, thereby excluding the endpoint rate allowed by previously established lower bounds. The proof assumes the endpoint rate as an upper bound near the blowup time and uses a result by Chae and Wolf to obtain a contradiction. The second result gives a BKM-type criterion for solutions to the incompressible Euler equations with variable coefficients in the minimal regularity class $H^r$, where $r \in (2.5,3)$.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Ingimarson

item.title: Rayleigh--Taylor instability and Hadamard ill-posedness for the rotating free-boundary Euler equations in three dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.15083v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The free-boundary incompressible Euler equations linearized at a rigidly rotating equilibrium on the flat product of the unit disk and a circle are Hadamard ill-posed in Sobolev spaces of order at least two. The equilibrium violates the Taylor sign condition, under which local well-posedness is known. Eulerian linearization retaining free-surface advection reduces the spectral problem to a modified Bessel equation; Rouch\'e's theorem yields an unstable root whose real part grows as the square root of the axial frequency. Eigenmode Sobolev norms grow as the corresponding power of that frequency. Rescaling gives data tending to zero whose solutions are unbounded at any prescribed positive time. At zero axial frequency the analysis recovers Ebin's rotating-disk rate (Communications in Partial Differential Equations 12 (1987), 1175--1201). The product lift gives nonlinear ill-posedness on the invariant class of axially independent data.
item.dc:creator: Chengchun Hao

item.title: Well-Posedness for the Cauchy Problem with Free Boundary in Half-Space Arising from Combustion Problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.15089v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we address the local-in-time well-posedness of an obstacle problem arising from a combustion model. The equation under consideration is a linear inhomogeneous heat equation on the moving domain $(s(t),\infty)$, subject to homogeneous Dirichlet and inhomogeneous Neumann boundary conditions. Our main result establishes the existence and uniqueness of a positive classical solution. Although several results are known for the homogeneous heat equation, much less is known about the inhomogeneous case. We show that the boundary function $s(t)$ is $\frac{1}{2}$-H\"older continuous in time when the forcing term has a singularity of order $O(1/\sqrt{t})$ as $t \to 0$. We also prove that if both the initial data and the forcing term are smooth, then $s$ has higher regularity than $\frac{1}{2}$-H\"older continuity.
item.dc:creator: Ken Furukawa, Yoshikazu Giga, Naoto Kajiwara

item.title: Solvability of $L^2$-Neumann Problems for Fractional Laplace Equations on Bounded Lipschitz Domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.15103v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $n\geq2$, $s\in(0,1)$, and $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain. In this paper, we study the solvability of the fractional Neumann problem \begin{equation*} \left\{\begin{aligned} (-\Delta)^su&=0 & & \text{in}\ \ \Omega,\\ \mathcal{N}_s u&=g & & \text{in}\ \ \mathbb{R}^n\setminus\Omega, \end{aligned}\right. \end{equation*} with $\mathcal{N}_s$ denoting the nonlocal normal derivative in $\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\Omega$ and $g:=a_sq$, where $a_s(z):=(1-s)\frac{\delta(z)^{-s}}{1+\delta(z)^{n+s}}$ with $\delta(z):=\mathrm{dist\,}(z,\partial\Omega)$ for any $z\in\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\Omega$, and $q\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\Omega,a_s\,dz)$ satisfies $\int_{\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\Omega}a_sq\,dz=0$. For the weak solution $u$, we obtain the non-tangential maximal function estimate \begin{equation*} \left\|\left(\delta^{1-s}|\nabla u|\right)^*\right\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\Omega,\,a_s\,dz)} \leq C\|q\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\Omega,\,a_s\,dz)}, \end{equation*} where, for any function $f$ on $\Omega$, $f^\ast$ denotes the non-tangential maximal function of $f$ on $\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\Omega$. This result extends the classical $L^2$ solvability theory for the Neumann problem of Laplace equations on bounded Lipschitz domains to the setting of fractional Neumann problems, and also provides a Neumann counterpart to the $L^2$-solvability result for fractional Dirichlet problems established by Colombo, Fern\'andez-Real and Ros-Oton \cite{CFR26}. In addition, we prove the fractional Sobolev estimate $\|u\|_{H^{3s/2}(\Omega)}\leq C\|q\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\Omega,\,a_s\,dz)}$ and the weighted gradient estimate \begin{equation*} \left(\int_\Omega\delta^{2-3s}|\nabla u|^2\,dx\right)^{\frac12} \leq C\|q\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\Omega,\,a_s\,dz)}. \end{equation*}
item.dc:creator: Wenxian Ma, Sibei Yang

item.title: Self-similar cusp formation in a large class of nonlocal transport equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.15174v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove finite-time gradient blow-up with sharp $C^{(5-b)/(b+3)}$ H\"older regularity for a class of nonlocal transport equations extending the $b$-family, for all real $1<b<5$. This class includes the Camassa--Holm and Degasperis--Procesi equations and, after rescaling, the generalized hyperelastic-rod wave equation. In the blow-up regime, the nonlocal equations reduce at leading order to the generalized Hunter--Saxton (gHS) equation with parameter $\ell=2/(b-1)$, whose self-similar scaling and corresponding profiles depend on $\ell$. Consequently, standard approaches tailored to a fixed self-similar profile cannot be applied directly. To handle this parameter dependence, we develop a general framework for self-similar singularity formation in evolution equations whose leading-order dynamics are governed by the gHS family. The key ingredient is a family of profile inequalities established for all real $\ell>1/2$, which we combine with a generalized maximum principle to close a parameter-dependent bootstrap argument. We identify model-specific hypotheses adapted to this framework, under which this argument yields the required stability estimates. This leads to a general theorem on singularity formation, which we apply to the entire class of nonlocal equations, thereby establishing finite-time gradient blow-up and sharp H\"older regularity. The theorem can also be applied to other evolution equations once the corresponding model-specific hypotheses are verified, without repeating the profile analysis or the common stability argument.
item.dc:creator: Yunjoo Kim, Bongsuk Kwon, Wanyong Shim

item.title: The Calder\'on Problem with Randomly Distributed Resonant Droplets
item.description: arXiv:2611.15196v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the recovery of an acoustic coefficient from boundary measurements made after the injection of a collection of small, highly contrasting droplets. This enters into the framework of quantitative ultrasound imaging using contrast agents. The centers are randomly distributed according to a prescribed strictly positive density $\rho\in C^1(\overline\Omega)$. We choose real incident frequencies near an active Newtonian resonance and prove a point-interaction approximation, followed by a comparison with the effective model $(-\Delta+P^2\rho-\omega^2n^2)u=0$. The constants are uniform as the amplitude $P^2$ increases, provided it is coupled to the size and distribution discrepancy of the droplets. A random rounding and displacement construction verifies the distribution assumption for each such given density. The effective Neumann-to-Dirichlet map is then linearized with a remainder of order $P^{-4}$. We derive reconstruction identities using complex geometrical optics solutions of the known reference operator $-\Delta+P^2\rho$. We also estimate the amplification of the boundary-map error in these identities and give a boundary integral correction for reconstruction from the full (and not the linearized) measured map.
item.dc:creator: Anjana E. J., Mourad Sini

item.title: Sharp Liouville theorems for the Hardy-H\'enon p-Laplace equation and classification of positive solutions for the critical Hardy p-Laplace equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.15282v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove subcritical nonexistence for $-\Delta_pu=|x|^au^q$ in $R^N$, with $1<p<N$ and $a>-p$, in the positive locally bounded weak class. Continuous Steiner symmetrization of a nonlinear auxiliary potential yields a directional pressure inequality; a localized Pohozaev identity and scaling give the Liouville theorem. At criticality, for $N\ge3$ and $-p<a<0$, we classify all positive entire weak solutions in $W^{1,p}_{\mathrm{loc}}(R^N)$, without assuming local boundedness, symmetry, stability, finite energy, or decay at infinity.
item.dc:creator: Haoyang Lu, Zhitao Zhang

item.title: Nonlinear selection in vanishing discount problems for Hamilton--Jacobi equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.15399v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the vanishing discount problem $G(x,Du_\lambda,\lambda u_\lambda)=c_0$, where $G$ is convex and superlinear in the momentum and strictly increasing in its last variable. Assuming a leading-order expansion of the Lagrangian of order $q>0$, we prove uniform convergence and characterize the selected solution by nonlinear inequalities against Mather measures. In particular, our results cover discount terms whose first derivative at the origin vanishes, such as the cubic discount, beyond existing convergence results based on first-order nondegeneracy. Our proof uses truncated calibrated curves and time averages, without the exponentially weighted measures used by Davini--Fathi--Iturriaga--Zavidovique. In the linear case, it gives a short alternative proof of their convergence and selection theorem. An example shows that linear and cubic discounts may select critical solutions that do not differ by an additive constant.
item.dc:creator: Panrui Ni, Maxime Zavidovique

item.title: The periodic Short-Pulse equation by the Riemann-Hilbert problem approach
item.description: arXiv:2611.15511v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we formulate a Riemann--Hilbert problem framework -- based on the Unified Transform Method (Fokas method) -- for the Short Pulse equation posed on a periodic domain. Under the stated spectral and reconstruction regularity assumptions, we show that a local solution of the periodic initial-value problem can be reconstructed from the solution of a suitably defined Riemann--Hilbert problem, whose jump data are explicitly characterized by spectral functions associated with the initial condition.
item.dc:creator: Iryna Karpenko, Dmitry Shepelsky, Gerald Teschl

item.title: Determination of a Bi-periodic Refractive Index for the Helmholtz Equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.15588v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate an inverse problem for the Helmholtz equation in a three-dimensional half-space with a biperiodic medium above a sound-soft plane. We establish the uniqueness of a real-valued, bounded, biperiodic refractive index that depends only on the horizontal variables using spectral techniques. %The frequency and quasiperiodicity parameter are fixed. An orthogonality identity is first derived from near-field measurements. By constructing suitable separated solutions, this identity is reduced to relations involving eigenfunctions of two-dimensional quasiperiodic Schr\"odinger operators. To recover Fourier information from these relations, we project horizontal plane waves onto suitable high-energy spectral subspaces, obtaining finite combinations of eigenfunctions that approximate the plane waves with a quantified error. Combining these approximations with the orthogonality identity, we show that all Fourier coefficients of the difference of two refractive indices vanish, thereby establishing the desired uniqueness.
item.dc:creator: Han Chen, Guanghui Hu

item.title: Calder\'on-Zygmund estimates and their failure for PDE with linear growth
item.description: arXiv:2611.15636v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate when Calder\'on-Zygmund estimates hold for PDEs of the type \[ \operatorname{div}(A(\nabla u)) = \operatorname{div}(F) \] where $A: \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2$ is a continuous map with linear growth. We show that, under natural assumptions, $L^p$-Calder\'on-Zygmund estimates hold for all $p \in (1,\infty)$ if and only if $v \mapsto \lim_{t \to \infty} A(tv)/t$ is linear and non-degenerate.
item.dc:creator: Armin Schikorra, Akshara Vincent

item.title: Asymptotic behaviors of solutions to the critical fractional $p$-Laplace equations with Hardy potential
item.description: arXiv:2611.15648v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we consider positive weak solutions $u\in\mathcal{D}^{s,p}(\mathbb{R}^{N})$ to the critical fractional $p$-Laplace equation with Hardy potential $(-\Delta_p)^s u-\mu\frac{u^{p-1}}{|x|^{ps}}=u^{p_s^{*}-1}$ in $\mathbb{R}^{N}$, where $N\geqslant 2$, $s\in(0,1)$, $p\in(1,\infty)$ satisfying $ps<N$, $p_s^{*}=\frac{Np}{N-ps}$ and $\mu\in(0,\mathcal{C}_{N,s,p})$, $\mathcal{C}_{N,s,p}$ denotes the sharp constant of the fractional Hardy inequality. By means of a suitable comparison principle for weak subsolutions and supersolutions of the equations $(-\Delta_p)^sf=\big(\frac{\mu}{|x|^{ps}}+a(x)\big)f^{p-1}$ on general open set $\Omega$, with nonzero exterior data and $a\in L^{\frac{N}{ps}}(\mathbb{R}^{N})$, combined with careful constructions of the weak subsolutions and supersolutions, we prove that every positive weak solution $u$ of the above problem satisfies $C^{-1}\leqslant|x|^{\mu_1}(1+|x|)^{\mu_2-\mu_1}u(x)\leqslant C$ for a.e. $x\in\mathbb{R}^{N}$, where $\mu_1<\mu_2$ are the two roots of the indicial equation associated with the Hardy operator and $C\in[1,\infty)$ depends on $u$. Also, we show that the constant $C$ cannot be chosen to depend only on $N$, $s$, $p$ and $\mu$.
item.dc:creator: Jungang Li, Yansheng Shen, Zeming Wang

item.title: Energy rigidity and weak--strong uniqueness for the anisotropic Navier--Stokes equations in $\mathbb{R}^2_+$
item.description: arXiv:2611.15703v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the two-dimensional incompressible Navier--Stokes equations with only horizontal dissipation in the upper half-plane $\mathbb{R}^2_+$. The combination of the missing directional regularity and the influence of the boundary presents an essential difficulty for the pressure estimates. We circumvent this difficulty by establishing an extension theorem for the weak formulation, based on the divergence-free condition and the homogeneous impermeability boundary condition. A key feature of this extension principle is that no boundary condition is required for the tangential velocity component. Consequently, every weak solution in the natural energy class on $\mathbb{R}^2_+$ admits a reflection extension that is a weak solution of the corresponding whole-space problem on $\mathbb{R}^2$. This extension allows us to transfer the energy rigidity and weak--strong uniqueness properties established by Demmel and Wiedemann \cite{E-W} to the half-plane setting. In particular, we prove the energy equality for weak solutions in the natural energy class and establish weak--strong uniqueness under the corresponding additional regularity assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Wenke Tan, Fan Wu

item.title: Dynamic Prandtl-Reuss Thermoplasticity with Degenerating Yield Constraints
item.description: arXiv:2611.15719v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a three-dimensional dynamic thermoplastic system with a temperature-dependent convex yield set whose deviatoric section may collapse completely at a finite temperature. The underlying constitutive model is rate-independent Prandtl-Reuss perfect plasticity, without Kelvin-Voigt viscosity, hardening, or a safe-load condition. We construct global approximation-generated relaxed entropy-energy states by a one-parameter Temam-Norton-Hoff-Galerkin scheme with an undiscretized heat equation and untruncated plastic heat production. The logarithmic temperature is strongly compact in $L^2(0,T;L^q(\Omega))$ for every $q<6$ and in $L^p((0,T)\times\Omega)$ for every $p<8/3$. An entropy-weighted work estimate yields convergence of the overstress at rate $O(\sqrt{\log n/n})$ in every fixed finite Lebesgue space and identifies stress admissibility. The constitutive limit comprises a distributional plastic balance, finite support-weighted measures, and compact-fibre lifts carrying exact normality and maximum plastic work. A locally finite lift on the positive-radius fibres unifies the level-restricted limits at every continuity level. At the macroscopic level, however, the available compactness does not identify a canonical stress-plastic-flow pairing. Moreover, an explicit smooth state satisfying the intrinsic relaxed balance conditions shows that these conditions do not imply macroscopic Prandtl-Reuss normality. In the fully collapsed regime, an energy-entropy rigidity argument determines the evolution and yields approximation-generated examples in which the plastic flow need not be a finite measure or the displacement need not retain its full boundary trace. Thermal concentration and plastic entropy production remain explicit throughout.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Owczarek

item.title: Strong and weak mean value sets for elliptic operators: uniqueness and counterexamples
item.description: arXiv:2611.15988v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Classical theorems of Epstein--Schiffer and Kuran characterize balls by the mean value identity for integrable harmonic functions. In the Fermi Lectures, Caffarelli described an obstacle problem construction of analogous averaging sets for symmetric uniformly elliptic divergence-form operators. Working in dimension $n \ge 2$ throughout the paper, we prove that for symmetric uniformly elliptic operators with bounded measurable coefficients, every bounded open set satisfying the mean value inequality for all integrable subsolutions defined on that set (what we call ``strong mean value sets'') agrees almost everywhere with the canonical set from Caffarelli's construction which has the same center and volume. The proof uses weak modified Schwarz potentials and an energy comparison. Additionally, we construct smooth symmetric uniformly elliptic operators for which the unit ball satisfies the mean value identity for all integrable solutions but fails the subsolution inequality, showing that there can be two distinct notions for what one can consider to be a ``mean value set.'' The canonical mean value set with the same center and volume as this weak mean value ball has a hole of positive measure.
item.dc:creator: Niles Armstrong, Ivan Blank

item.title: Blow-up rate for 1-d semilinear wave equations without scaling invariance at characteristic points
item.description: arXiv:2611.16004v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the blow-up behavior of solutions to the semilinear wave equation $$ \partial_t^2 u - \partial_x^2 u = |u|^{p-1}u \ln^a(u^2+2), \quad (x,t)\in \mathbb{R} \times [0,T), $$ with $p > 1$ and $a<0$. While the blow-up rate at non-characteristic points was determined for all $a \in \mathbb{R}$ in previous work, the analysis at characteristic points has remained an open problem. The main obstruction is that known constructions of a Lyapunov functional in similarity variables require several steps and rely on a covering argument, which is not available at characteristic points. Focusing on the regime $a < 0$, we construct a Lyapunov functional directly, without any covering argument. This yields uniform bounds on the solution in similarity variables, and hence the blow-up rate at every point, including characteristic ones. To our knowledge, this is the first work to determine the blow-up rate at characteristic points for an equation without scaling invariance.
item.dc:creator: M. A. Hamza, H. Zaag

item.title: Evolution of Internal Waves on Surfaces of Revolution with Flat Ends
item.description: arXiv:2611.16112v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We generalize the 2D linear internal wave equation to non-compact surfaces of revolution with flat ends. We show that the leading profile of this equation with oscillatory forcing is the unique incoming solution to the corresponding stationary equation. This is done by proving a limiting absorption principle via propagation of semiclassical defect measure.
item.dc:creator: Lakshay Patel

item.title: Maximum Principles and Principal Eigenvalue for Coupled Local/Nonlocal Models
item.description: arXiv:2611.16131v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we analyze the validity of the maximum principle and the existence of a principal eigenvalue for a problem involving two regions, in one of them the main operator is the classical Laplacian (a local operator) while in the other region the operator is a nonlocal one (these regions are coupled via a transmission term that is also nonlocal). The main difficulty here comes from the lack of compactness of the nonlocal part that occurs since we are considering non-singular kernels.
item.dc:creator: Willian Cintra, J\^onatas Peralta, Julio D. Rossi, Antonio Su\'arez

item.title: Global-in-time dynamics of the pressureless Euler/incompressible non-Newtonian equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.16319v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper addresses a two-phase fluid system on the periodic domain $\mathbb{T}^3$, consisting of the pressureless Euler equations and the incompressible non-Newtonian equations coupled through a drag force. We prove the global-in-time existence of strong solutions to this system for a certain class of stress tensors in the non-Newtonian fluid. Our proof combines a priori large-time behavior estimates for classical solutions with a bootstrapping argument on the $L^2$-Sobolev norms, which effectively handles the difficulties caused by the lack of dissipation in the density of the Euler equation.
item.dc:creator: Jinwook Jung, Subin Kim

item.title: Sharp low-dimensional Constants in the second-order hydrogen Heisenberg uncertainty principle via Jacobi chains
item.description: arXiv:2611.16353v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish the sharp constants $\mathcal H_N$ of the second-order Hydrogen Heisenberg uncertainty principle for $N=2,3$. Starting from the first angular mode reduction, we rewrite the fourth-order radial quotient as two coupled radial Coulomb channels. Then we turn the compatibility constraint into an explicit Jacobi chain by expanding the $B$-channel in generalized Laguerre polynomials and passing to parity-tail variables. Its tail energies satisfy scalar Riccati recursions, equivalently continued fractions. Furthermore, we characterize $2\mathcal H_2$ and $2\mathcal H_3$ as the unique roots of two explicit scalar equations, and we show that free-tail and Dirichlet finite sections provide monotone lower and upper approximations converging to the sharp constants. This yields rigorous bounds and the values $$\mathcal H_2\approx0.84478056,\quad \mathcal H_3\approx1.82348779.$$ We also obtain uniqueness of the first-mode radial extremizer up to amplitude, rotation, and dilation.
item.dc:creator: Xia Huang, Dong Ye

item.title: Energy gaps for critical Dirac equations on spheres
item.description: arXiv:2611.16355v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the critical Dirac equation \[ D\psi=H(x)|\psi|^{\frac{2}{m-1}}\psi \] on the round sphere $\mbs^m$, $m\ge2$, where $D$ is the Dirac operator. For $H\equiv1$, the ground-state energy $E_m=\frac{m^{m-1}}{2^{m+1}}\vol(\mbs^m)$ depends only on the dimension $m$. In dimension two, the nonzero solution energies are exactly $\pi,3\pi,4\pi,\ldots$. For $m\ge3$, we prove a gap $(E_m,(1+\Ga_m)E_m)$ above the ground-state energy and give bounds for its optimal relative size $\Ga_m$. For positive $H$, let $\tau_H=E_m/(\max H)^{m-1}$ be the first bubble energy. If $m\ge3$, every $H$ in a residual subset of the positive $C^1$ functions admits solutions with infinitely many distinct weighted energies in $(\tau_H,\min\{2,1+\Ga_m\}\tau_H)$ tending to $\tau_H$. Along a subsequence these solutions form a single ground-state bubble at a global maximum of $H$. For each $k\ge1$, smooth positive coefficients admitting at least $k$ distinct energies in this interval are dense among positive functions in $C^1$ and $W^{2,s}$, $m/2<s<\infty$. In the $C^2$ topology, however, an open set of positive coefficients admits only the trivial solution. We approximate a smooth $H_*$ in this set by smooth positive $H_j$ in every $C^{1,\al}$ and $W^{2,s}$ with $0<\al<1$ and $1\le s<\infty$. Solutions for $H_j$ form a single bubble at the unique maximum of $H_*$ as their weighted energies tend to $\tau_{H_*}$.
item.dc:creator: Tian Xu

item.title: Critical mass for infinite-time blow-up in a Keller-Segel system with indirect signal production on closed Riemannian surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.16572v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a parabolic-elliptic-ODE chemotaxis system with indirect signal production on closed connected Riemannian surfaces. For all sufficiently regular nonnegative initial data, the system admits a unique global classical solution. We show that the solution remains globally bounded if the total mass $M<8\pi$. For each $M>8\pi$, we find initial data of mass $M$ that yield infinite-time blow-up solutions. We then adapt the argument to the corresponding Neumann problem in a smooth bounded planar domain and obtain infinite-time blow-up solutions for any mass $M>4\pi$. At the critical mass $M=8\pi$, we show that the solutions are globally bounded on spheres equipped with the canonical spherical metric, and we construct a solution blowing up in infinite time on the Riemann sphere equipped with a special metric.
item.dc:creator: Jing Li, Yuxiang Li

item.title: Recovering Small Perturbations of a Known Inclusion from One Mixed Steklov Eigenpair with Local Boundary Data
item.description: arXiv:2611.16596v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the recovery of small normal displacements of a known inclusion from a single mixed Steklov eigenpair. The data consist of the eigenvalue and the eigenfunction trace on any nonempty open subset of the fixed outer boundary, with the eigenfunction normalized using only that subset. For an inner Dirichlet condition, we prove that the linearized measurement map is injective at every simple eigenvalue. A compatible adjoint identity yields a reconstruction method with a conditional stability estimate on any fixed finite-dimensional space of smooth displacements. For the principal Dirichlet eigenpair, the same local data also determine the inclusion uniquely among sufficiently small normal graphs. In a three-dimensional concentric shell, the eigenvalue determines the mean displacement at first order, while spherical harmonics diagonalize the remaining full-boundary trace map. The singular values decay exponentially with harmonic degree, yielding logarithmic conditional stability under a Sobolev prior. Numerical experiments using the perturbed geometry illustrate the quadratic linearization error and the deterioration of conditioning as the observed patch shrinks. For an inner Neumann condition, we prove linearized injectivity at every positive simple eigenvalue.
item.dc:creator: Jiho Hong

item.title: Optimal control for an anisotropic Stokes-Nernst-Planck-Poisson system
item.description: arXiv:2611.16615v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study an optimal control problem aimed at enhancing mixing in anisotropic electrolytes described by an instationary Stokes-Nernst-Planck-Poisson system in three space dimensions, where the anisotropy is encoded by a given director field in the diffusion and permittivity matrices. The control is the external electric potential entering through the Robin boundary condition of the Poisson equation. The cost functional combines tracking-type terms for the charge concentrations and an $L^2$-regularization of the control with a negative vorticity term that favors rotational flow. Assuming that the diffusion and permittivity matrices coincide, we first prove existence and uniqueness of weak solutions with nonnegative, essentially bounded concentrations, together with Lipschitz continuous dependence on the control. Since, through the negative vorticity term, the cost functional is no longer weakly lower semicontinuous, existence of an optimal control relies on strong convergence of the velocity gradients. Finally, we prove Fr\'echet differentiability of the control-to-state operator, introduce the adjoint system, and derive first-order necessary optimality conditions in the form of a variational inequality.
item.dc:creator: Giulia Cavalleri, Luisa Plato

item.title: Variational approximation by complex Gaussians for the nonlinear logarithmic equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.16640v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the semiclassical logarithmic Schr{\"o}dinger equation, with an at most quadratic potential and with Gaussian initial states. For a critical nonlinear term in the semiclassical regime, we analyze an approximation based on the variational evolution of Gaussian wave packets. We also prove a nonlinear superposition principle for solutions issued from the sum of two Gaussian wave packets initially localized at distinct points in phase space. For both a single Gaussian wave packet and a superposition of two Gaussian wave packets, we compare the variational approximation with the standard coherent-state approximation and highlight their respective features. The required assumptions are weakened in this setting without becoming technically involved.
item.dc:creator: Marianne Curely (UA, LAREMA), Lysianne Hari (UMLP, LMB)

item.title: Refined critical flux bounds for Leray's problem in a pipe with the Navier-slip boundary
item.description: arXiv:2611.16668v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study uniqueness for stationary incompressible Navier--Stokes flows in infinite pipes with the Navier-slip boundary. For a cylindrical pipe of unit radius and a positive friction ratio, uniqueness holds when $|\Phi|\leq 2\pi\sqrt{40/7}\approx 15$. This significantly improves upon the result of the first author, Liu and Zhou (J. Differential Equations 461:114108, 2026) where the uniqueness requires $|\Phi|\leq \pi/16\approx 0.2$. For small positive friction ratio $\alpha$, this flux condition can be improved to $|\Phi|\leq 4\sqrt{2}\,\pi^2/\alpha$. For an infinite pipe with a bounded, smooth, simply connected cross-section $\Sigma$, we prove uniqueness for every $0<\alpha<\infty$ provided that $|\Phi|\leq c_\Sigma(1+\alpha)/\alpha$, where $c_\Sigma>0$ depends only on $\Sigma$.
item.dc:creator: Zijin Li, Zhipeng Wu

item.title: The coercivity conjecture for nonlocal energies
item.description: arXiv:2611.16682v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The coercivity conjecture for nonlocal energies asks whether uniform ellipticity implies $H^s$-coercivity for symmetric nonlocal kernels of order $2s$, with $0<s<1$. We show that the conjecture fails whenever $n>2s$ for every $s \in (0,1)$ and $n \geq 1$, even for smooth compactly supported test functions; for $n=1$ and $s>1/2$, we show that it holds. The construction also gives bounded discontinuous weak solutions in $H^s_{\rm loc}$ to nonlocal equations in divergence form with kernels in this class. Despite the failure, we show that the conjecture holds for several important classes of kernels. We establish a general local coercivity criterion based on annular cancellation, which applies in particular to kernels satisfying both divergence- and nondivergence-form symmetry. The criterion also allows us to treat kernels comparable to stable kernels with bounded measurable coefficients, as well as non-cutoff Boltzmann kernels under a geometric nonconcentration assumption. As an application, we obtain a short and self-contained proof of the Gressman--Strain anisotropic coercivity estimate. Furthermore, by combining our new criterion with existing regularity results, we obtain H\"older estimates under ellipticity and cancellation assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Linus Behn, Roberto Colombo, Xavier Fern\'andez-Real, Florian Grube, Harsh Prasad, Xavier Ros-Oton

item.title: An Analytic Toroidal MHD Equilibrium with Trivial Euclidean Symmetry Group
item.description: arXiv:2611.16688v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide a method to construct a real-analytic ideal MHD equilibrium $(B,p)$ in a solid toroidal domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^{3}$, with $B$ tangential to the boundary $\partial\Omega$. The regular pressure level sets foliate $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$ by nested tori surrounding a magnetic axis $\Gamma$, with $\nabla p\neq0$ away from the axis. We construct an example where the magnetic field is nonvanishing on $\Omega$, and the rotational transform equals 2 on every regular pressure surface. The equilibrium has a trivial Euclidean symmetry group. It is non-isolated in the sense that it belongs to a real-analytic one-parameter family connecting it to an axisymmetric equilibrium. The toroidal domain, magnetic field and pressure vary smoothly along this family. Under the MHD--Euler correspondence, the construction also yields a real-analytic steady incompressible Euler flow with a nonconstant Bernoulli function. This constructively disproves one formulation of Grad's conjecture by exhibiting a smooth toroidal MHD equilibrium with nested pressure surfaces whose Euclidean symmetry group is trivial.
item.dc:creator: Kooper de Lacy, Naoki Sato

item.title: Asymptotic stability of self-similar blow-up for the two-dimensional Zakharov system
item.description: arXiv:2611.16731v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove asymptotic stability of the small-parameter Glangetas-Merle self-similar blow-up solutions of the two-dimensional Zakharov system under nonradial perturbations in the energy space. The proof establishes dissipation on the wave time scale by canceling the fast density coupling. We impose nonlinear orthogonality to the ground state of the density-dependent Schr\"odinger operator for modulation and use successive energy corrections after subtracting the instantaneous density response from the Schr\"odinger error. The resulting dissipation yields power-law decay of the rescaled errors in the Schr\"odinger gradient, weighted local mass, and wave energy norms.
item.dc:creator: Tej-eddine Ghoul, Jie Liu, Nader Masmoudi

item.title: Existence, Nonexistence, and Regularity Results for Supercritical Quasilinear Elliptic Problems with Hardy Potential
item.description: arXiv:2611.16754v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the existence of solutions to the following supercritical elliptic problem involving the $p$-Laplace operator and the Hardy-Leray potential \begin{equation*} \left\{\begin{array}{rcll} -\Delta_p u +u^\beta|\nabla u|^p &= & {\vartheta} \dfrac{u^q }{|x|^p}+ f\;\; &\hbox{in } \Omega u &\geq & 0\;\; &\hbox{in } \Omega u &= & 0\;\;&\hbox{on } \partial\Omega, \end{array}\right. \end{equation*} where $0\in\Omega$. We analyze the effect of the perturbation term $u^\beta|\nabla u|^p$, with $\beta \geq 0$, and the role of the exponent $q$ on the existence of solutions. We also analyze nonexistence of solutions when $f$ is a singular measure. Finally, we focus on the regularity and asymptotic properties of these solutions.
item.dc:creator: Boumediene Abdellaoui, Susana Merch\'an, Luigi Montoro

item.title: Eventual Collisional Relaxation After Large Echo-Driven Amplification in a Weakly Collisional Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck System
item.description:
arXiv:2611.16761v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the weakly collisional Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck system near a Maxwellian equilibrium and construct global classical solutions exhibiting large transient growth before eventual collisional relaxation. The main mechanism is a nonlinear plasma-echo cascade which remains effective up to the enhanced-dissipation time scale $t\sim
u^{- rac13}$, producing norm inflation of size larger than $
u^{-1}$ from arbitrarily small $
u$-dependent perturbations. At the same time, the nonzero spatial modes decay at the enhanced-dissipation scale $e^{-r
u^{ rac13}t}$, while the zero mode relaxes at the thermal scale $e^{-
u t}$. The estimates also reveal a sharp contrast in the smoothing effects before and after the collisional time scale $t\sim 
u^{-1}$. As a consequence, our construction gives explicit upper bounds on the Sobolev and Gevrey stability thresholds: perturbations of the corresponding $
u$-dependent sizes can still trigger severe echo-driven amplification before collisional dissipation becomes dominant at the critical time scale $t\sim
u^{- rac13}$.
item.dc:creator: Luo Yue

item.title: Observability from Measurable Sets for Heat Equations with Bounded Space-Time Potentials
item.description: arXiv:2611.16811v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish final-state observability for heat equations with real-valued bounded space--time potentials on bounded $C^2$ domains, from arbitrary measurable space--time sets of positive measure. On $\mathbb R^n$, we prove observability from time-dependent sets whose spatial slices are uniformly thick on a set of times of positive measure. A counterexample for the free heat equation on $\mathbb R$ shows that integral thickness alone is insufficient for observability.
item.dc:creator: Ming Wang, Can Zhang

item.title: On the quasi-static growth of cavities in incompressible elastomers
item.description: arXiv:2611.16854v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a variational model of incompressible elastomers exhibiting cavitation, we establish the existence of irreversible quasi-static evolutions driven by time-dependent boundary conditions. Our result extends previous work by Mora-Corral (2014) to incompressible materials under weaker regularity assumptions on the boundary datum. The proof employs the multiplicative splitting introduced by Francfort and Mielke (2006) to reduce the problem to time-independent boundary conditions and then invokes abstract results on the existence of energetic solutions to rate-independent systems. Specifically, the construction of mutual recovery sequences requires particular attention to accommodate the incompressibility constraint: to this end we employ the method by Moser (1965) to exhibit incompressible diffeomorphisms interpolating between localized translations and the identity.
item.dc:creator: Marco Bresciani, Giuliano Lazzaroni

item.title: Cavity collapse and vorticity gradient blow-up in free-boundary Euler flow
item.description: arXiv:2611.16868v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct smooth solutions of the three-dimensional incompressible free-boundary Euler equations with surface tension whose vorticity remains bounded while its full spatial gradient blows up in finite time. The solutions are axisymmetric without swirl and occupy bounded domains in which a tubular cavity collapses onto a circle at time $T$, while the outer free surface converges smoothly. The vorticity $\omega$ can be chosen arbitrarily small in $L^\infty$, uniformly up to collapse, and satisfies $\|\nabla\omega(t)\|_{L^\infty}\asymp (T-t)^{-1/2}|\log(T-t)|^{1/4}$ as $t\uparrow T$. A nonconstant material trace of the relative vorticity on the shrinking surface determines direction-dependent limits of the terminal vorticity, which therefore has no continuous extension across the collapse circle. The kinetic energy measure converges to the sum of a uniform line measure on this circle and a nonzero bulk part carried by a bounded rotational field. The construction couples vorticity transport to the boundary dynamics through weighted estimates in the collapsing collar and a cancellation in the normal acceleration.
item.dc:creator: Tao Luo, Siqi Yang

item.title: Gradient stability for the Sobolev inequality with optimal dimensional dependence
item.description: arXiv:2611.16946v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Figalli and Zhang [29] established gradient stability for the sharp Sobolev inequality with the optimal exponent $r_p=\max\{2,p\}$. We prove that, for every fixed $p>1$, the corresponding optimal stability constant $\mathsf C_{n,p}$ admits effective upper and lower bounds of order $n^{-1}$ for all integers $n>p$. In particular, the dimensional dependence $n^{-1}$ is optimal. Our result extends the optimal dimensional dependence established for $p=2$ by Dolbeault, Esteban, Figalli, Frank, and Loss [18] to every $p>1$.
item.dc:creator: Yuxuan Zhou, Wenming Zou

item.title: Off-diagonal decay of capacitance matrices via Brownian motion
item.description: arXiv:2611.16978v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish upper and lower bounds for the off-diagonal entries of the capacitance matrix of infinite systems of spherical resonators in chain, screen and crystal geometries. Let $d$ denote the distance between two resonator centres. For chains contained in a cylinder of bounded radius and with bounded axial gaps, the decay is of order $d^{-1}\log^{-2}(2+d)$. For screens contained in a slab and relatively dense in the tangential directions, it is of order $d^{-3}$. For relatively dense three-dimensional configurations, we obtain exponential upper and lower bounds. No periodicity is assumed. Our proofs are based on the classical connection between the Dirichlet problem and Brownian motion, which enables us to relate the decay estimates to hitting probabilities of Brownian motion.
item.dc:creator: Habib Ammari, Clemens Thalhammer

item.title: How to arrange four points in the plane
item.description: arXiv:2611.16990v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Arranging points in the plane appears to be an elementary geometric problem, yet it is deeply rooted in statistical physics. As a toy model, we consider the configuration of four points. We completely classify the minimal configurations of four points interaction energy in $\R^2$ under the general Lennard-Jones potentials $V(r)=r^{-p}-br^{-q}$, where $p>q>0$ and $b\in\R$. We find that there is a threshold curve \[ D_{p,q}=2^{-(p-q)/2}\Bigl(1+\frac{p-q}{q+2}\bigl(1+2^{-(q+2)/2}\bigr)\Bigr) \] to determine the minimal shapes. The main results can be stated concisely as follows: consider $\min\sum_{1\le i<j\le4}\bigl(|x_i-x_j|^{-p}-b|x_i-x_j|^{-q}\bigr)$. For $b\le0$, the minimizer does not exist. For $b>0$, the minimizer is unique up to rotation and translation. Furthermore, the minimizer is \[ \begin{cases} \text{a square},&\hbox{if}\;\; D_{p,q}\ge1, \text{a rhombus with angle }\theta\in(\pi/3,\pi/2),&\hbox{if}\;\; D_{p,q}<1. \end{cases} \]
item.dc:creator: Senping Luo

item.title: Macroscopic $L^\infty$ bounds for the homogeneous Landau--Coulomb equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.17000v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish an instantaneous global $L^\infty(\R^3)$ bound at positive times for smooth, rapidly decaying solutions to the three-dimensional spatially homogeneous Landau equation with Coulomb potential, where the upper bound depends solely on the initial mass, momentum, energy, and entropy. This resolves an open problem posed by Golding, Gualdani, and Loher \cite{GGL} without requiring any initial higher velocity moments, Fisher information, or Lebesgue integrability. The proof builds on two main analytical ingredients. First, we establish the instantaneous generation of the negatively weighted Fisher information with weight $\la{v}^{-1}$. On the lifted two-particle phase space, we compare the separable weight matrix against a collision-invariant pair weight and control the rotational commutator near the diagonal via the quadratic local mass decay supplied by the conserved energy, closing a Riccati differential inequality at the second-moment threshold. Second, to overcome the $\la{v}^{-3}$ radial degeneracy of the diffusion matrix at large velocities, we prove a truncated anisotropic mixed Nash inequality on upper level sets of the density that recovers longitudinal regularity from two transverse Fisher directions and the nonlinear high-density part of the Coulomb entropy dissipation. Localizing this functional inequality to radially aligned velocity cells with the critical weight $\la{v}^{3/2}$ and coupling it with a weighted truncated entropy identity across nested exterior domains yields a superlinear De Giorgi recurrence that bounds the velocity tail uniformly in $\R^3$.
item.dc:creator: Lingda Xu

item.title: On a PDE-ODE-ODE model for meniscus tissue regeneration with space-dependent, possibly degenerate diffusion tensor
item.description: arXiv:2611.17063v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate a tissue regeneration model that describes the coupled dynamics of human mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs), chondrocytes, and newly formed extracellular matrix (ECM). The system features motility terms only for the mesenchymal stem cells, more precisely myopic diffusion and haptotaxis towards increasing ECM; all of those terms involve a space-dependent, possibly degenerating tensor. The chondrocytes are obtained from MSCs by differentiation and provide positive feedback to MSCs via dedifferentiation. The considered macroscopic model was obtained by upscaling from a formulation within the kinetic theory of active particles. Under appropriate assumptions we prove global existence of classical solutions in 2D and 3D in the case of a nondegenerating tensor and global existence of weak solutions in 2D when the diffusion tensor is allowed to degenerate. Numerical simulations are performed in 2D in order to illustrate the solution behavior.
item.dc:creator: Nishith Mohan, Ahmad Hussein, Bernd Simeon, Christina Surulescu

item.title: Discrete unique continuation for Schr\"odinger equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.17073v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study discrete unique continuation for one-dimensional Schr\"odinger equations. We prove that if a solution vanishes at the points $\pm n^{\alpha}$ at time $0$ and at the points $\pm n^{\beta}$ at time $1$, it must vanish identically in two main cases: the case of a Schr\"odinger equation with a real potential that is uniformly of Gevrey class $\sigma\ge 0$ in space, provided that $\max\{1,\sigma\}\big(\alpha/(1-\alpha)+\beta/(1-\beta)\big)<1$, and in the case of the cubic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation, provided that $\alpha/(1-\alpha)+\beta/(1-\beta)<1$. Unlike previous results for logarithmically spaced zeros, our methods do not rely on complex analysis. We first show that, whenever $\alpha+\beta<1$, the zeros force the solution to lie in the Schwartz class at all times. We then convert the zeros into gaussian decay at the two times, by combining energy estimates for iterations of the vector field $\Gamma=x+2it\partial_x$ with techniques from Fourier uniqueness problems, and conclude with the Morgan-type uncertainty principle of Escauriaza, Kenig, Ponce and Vega.
item.dc:creator: Torunn S. Jensen, Didier Pilod, Jo\~ao P. G. Ramos

item.title: Mixed Inner Variation and Global Hessian Integrability for Degenerate Monge-Amp\`ere Equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.17088v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the global Hessian integrability for nonzero convex solutions of the degenerate Monge-Amp\`ere equations $\det D^2u=M(-u)^p$ with zero boundary values on arbitrary bounded convex domains in $\mathbb{R}^n$ in the global Lipschitz regime $p>n-2$. We establish global $W^{2,1+\varepsilon}$ estimates for every $0<\varepsilon<\min\{(p-n+2)/n,1\}$ and determine the optimal range of $\varepsilon$ in dimension two. The flat faces of rectangular boxes and their intersections impose upper bounds on the admissible exponents of global Hessian integrability. A new input in the proof for general dimensions is a Caccioppoli-type estimate for the boundary Hessian mass using vector fields arising from a mixed second inner variation. For the sharp higher integrability result in the plane, we use the combined hodograph-Legendre transform to control the curvature of level sets.
item.dc:creator: Nam Q. Le

item.title: Convergence rates for smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) with nonlinear pressure
item.description: arXiv:2611.17151v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish quantitative convergence results for the smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) method approximating the compressible Euler equations with nonlinear pressure laws $\rho^\gamma$, $\gamma\geq 2$. Our approach is based on a nonlocal approximation of the pressure force that preserves the energy structure of the original system, including an exact energy balance. Using the relative entropy method, we prove convergence towards smooth solutions of the compressible Euler equations as the nonlocality parameter $\varepsilon\to0$, with algebraic convergence rates and an explicit algebraic relationship between $\varepsilon$ and the number of particles $N$. In particular, we obtain quantitative convergence rates for the density in the Wasserstein distance and negative Sobolev norms, and for the momentum in the flat metric. A key feature of our analysis is that it applies to measure-valued densities in the nonlocal system, providing a unified framework for both continuum and particle solutions. Our results extend the existing rigorous convergence theory for SPH beyond quadratic pressure ($\gamma=2$) to general nonlinear pressure laws with $\gamma\geq 2$ on the periodic domain.
item.dc:creator: Piotr Gwiazda, Jakub Skrzeczkowski, Jakub Wo\'znicki

item.title: Higher integrability for parabolic $p$-Laplace equations with gradient-dependent sources
item.description: arXiv:2611.17154v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper aims to establish higher gradient integrability away from the initial time for solutions to parabolic $p$-Laplace equations with general gradient-dependent lower-order terms throughout the singular and degenerate regimes. For this purpose, we develop an elliptic reconstruction argument based on an $L^2$-valued temporal H\"{o}lder estimate, thereby transferring the problem to elliptic estimates and quantitative control of the reconstruction error. In particular, our approach yields an explicit higher-integrability exponent. We further construct counterexamples illustrating that bounded continuous initial data alone are insufficient to ensure higher gradient integrability up to the initial time. Finally, we provide counterexamples demonstrating that gradient-dependent lower-order terms can prevent temporal Lipschitz regularity.
item.dc:creator: Yan Li, Zhiwen Zhao

item.title: Qualitative properties of solutions to anisotropic parabolic equations: Part III- H\"{o}lder continuity
item.description: arXiv:2611.17203v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we study the local H\"older continuity of non-negative solutions to a class of doubly nonlinear anisotropic partial differential equations, with prototype \[ u_t-\sum_{i=1}^N D_i\Big(|D_i u^{m_i}|^{p_i-2}D_i u^{m_i}\Big)=0, \quad m_i>0,\quad p_i>1,\quad i=1,\ldots,N. \] The main result shows that, when the exponents describing the diffusion in different spatial directions are sufficiently close to one another, the solutions enjoy local H\"older continuity. A key feature of the analysis is the distinction between two diffusion regimes: the degenerate and the singular cases; the local regularity results are established in both regimes, under suitable conditions on the exponents.
item.dc:creator: Simone Ciani, Eurica Henriques, Maria O. Savchenko, Igor I. Skrypnik

item.title: Radiation and persistent shape dynamics for the five-dimensional energy-critical nonlinear wave equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.17243v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the nonradial five-dimensional focusing energy-critical wave equation. We construct a forward-global solution which remains arbitrarily close to a nondegenerate sign-changing stationary state in the energy space and is asymptotic to a varying stationary profile plus one free wave. The stationary profile moves in a compact conformal family, but its limit set contains a continuum of classes modulo translations, dilations and rotations. Consequently, the solution admits no soliton resolution using a fixed finite collection of stationary profiles and fixed Lorentz velocities, with pairwise orthogonal spatial parameters. That is, we disprove the fixed-profile soliton resolution conjecture for the five-dimensional focusing energy-critical wave equation. The construction uses a sequence of incoming waves with summable energies. Their quadratic impulses produce fixed shape displacements on increasing time scales. The main estimates control the zero eigenvalue of the linearized operator and the nonlinear error uniformly over the entire sequence. The stationary input uses a computer-assisted spectral bound for a symmetric single-node state.
item.dc:creator: Xuwen Chen, Justin Holmer, Shunlin Shen

item.title: A counterexample to fixed-profile soliton resolution for the three-dimensional quintic wave equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.17291v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the three-dimensional focusing energy-critical wave equation. We construct a bounded forward-global solution which starts arbitrarily close to a sign-changing stationary state and is asymptotic to a varying stationary profile plus one free wave. The core has two limits in distinct similarity orbits. A single energy-space norm identity identifies the radiation and reduces every competing fixed list to one profile; the two limits then give a contradiction. The construction uses summable radiation packets whose quadratic impulses produce fixed shape displacements on increasing time scales. We control the nonlinear error uniformly over these intervals and select the endpoints by a compact fixed-point map. A computer-assisted certificate validates the stationary state and its complete odd energy kernel.
item.dc:creator: Xuwen Chen, Justin Holmer, Shunlin Shen

item.title: $C^{1,\alpha}$ Regularity of $W^{2,2}$ $Q$-Valued Maps with Small Laplacian
item.description: arXiv:2611.17317v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a regularity criterion for $Q$-valued maps $u\in W^{2,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega,\mathcal A_Q(\mathbb R^k))$, where $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ is open. If $|\Delta u|\leq\delta_*|D^2u|$ almost everywhere, with $\delta_*=\delta_*(n,k,Q)>0$ sufficiently small, then $u\in C^{1,\alpha}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ for some $\alpha=\alpha(n,k,Q)>0$, with quantitative estimates. The result holds for arbitrary $n\geq2$, $k\geq1$, and $Q\geq1$. The proof establishes uniform energy decay using a rigidity principle for positive-semidefinite matrix-valued measures with an aperture bound and approximately atomic divergence, extending the target-stress argument for the homogeneity gap in \cite{Luc26}. The argument relies only on first variation identities. As consequences, we obtain $C^{1,\alpha}$ regularity for Dirichlet-stationary $W^{2,2}$ maps and for locally Lipschitz $W^{2,2}$ maps whose graph varifolds are stationary and have sufficiently small slope. Combining the latter result with Bellettini's Lipschitz sheeting theorem \cite{Bel25}, we establish $C^{1,\alpha}$ sheeting in the multiple-valued sense for two-sided stable minimal immersions whose singular set has vanishing $2$-capacity relative to the immersion, under suitable flatness and mass bounds. Our results allow us to reduce the proof of compactness within this class, under locally uniform mass bounds, to the conjecture that branch sets of stationary $C^{1,\alpha}$ multiple-valued graphs in codimension one have vanishing $2$-capacity.
item.dc:creator: Mattia Luchese

item.title: The Isoperimetric Flow and Synthetic Scalar Curvature for Causal Variational Principles
item.description: arXiv:2611.14265v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: An isoperimetric flow is introduced in the setting of causal variational principles. Describing the whole space by the support of a minimizing measure, we define an area functional on subsets by a surface layer integral. Mean curvature is defined via the first variation of this area functional. Using the method of minimizing movement, the isoperimetric flow is constructed as a Lipschitz curve of measures with prescribed volume change. As illustrating examples, we introduce and analyze ``smeared variants'' of the mean curvature flow in Euclidean space and on a Riemannian manifold. In these examples, it is shown that our area functional coincides with the usual area up to specified curvature corrections. As an application of our general results, by analyzing the volume and area of small isoperimetric balls, we introduce notions of local dimension and synthetic scalar curvature.
item.dc:creator: Felix Finster, Franz Gmeineder, Margarita Kraus

item.title: Sharp partition function bound for the attractive logarithmic gas
item.description: arXiv:2611.14914v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For the attractive logarithmic potential, we prove that the partition function is bounded uniformly in the number of particles on every compact inverse-temperature interval $[0,\be_0]$ with $\be_0<B$, where $B\in(0,2\d]$ is the sharp constant in the logarithmic Hardy--Littlewood--Sobolev inequality. The proof separates a smooth bulk, which inherits the entropy inequality, from a short-range singular interaction. The singular contribution is controlled on the event that each box of a fixed grid contains few particles. The complementary overcrowding event has exponentially small probability, which compensates a crude linear-in-$N$ bound on the log partition function. The resulting estimate supplies the partition bound that can be used recycled in a few different results. A separate Lean formalization verifies the conditional partition-bound theorem under the log-HLS assumption.
item.dc:creator: Matias G. Delgadino, Matthew Rosenzweig, Rishabh Gvalani

item.title: Uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for the Kuramoto model on the sphere
item.description: arXiv:2611.15015v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish quantitative uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for a generalization of the classical Kuramoto model on spheres of arbitrary dimension. For $n$ particles that are initialized independently from a probability measure with an $L^p$ density, $p>1$, and a nonzero mean vector, we obtain an explicit high-probability bound for the supremum over all times of the Wasserstein distance between the empirical and mean-field distributions. In sufficiently high dimension, this bound has the same order as the standard empirical sampling rate on the sphere and is therefore optimal. The proof combines a finite-time propagation of chaos estimate, a quantitative synchronization result for the mean-field model, and a late-time stability estimate of the system.
item.dc:creator: Shi Chen, Zhengjiang Lin, Emre Parmaksiz

item.title: Strict Monotonicity of the First Positive Steklov Eigenvalue on Eccentric Spherical Shells in Every Dimension
item.description: arXiv:2611.15063v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For $d\ge2$, consider the region between two nested spheres of fixed radii, with the inner sphere translated a distance $\varepsilon$ from the outer center. We prove that the first positive eigenvalue of the Steklov problem, with the spectral boundary condition imposed on both spheres, decreases strictly with $\varepsilon$ throughout the noncontact interval. This settles the planar monotonicity conjecture formulated by Nigam and establishes its higher-dimensional counterparts. In dimension two we use a double-center holomorphic expansion and a pair of positive compact coefficient operators. For every $d\ge3$, solid Gegenbauer harmonics yield analogous axisymmetric and transverse operators, with a positive rank-one monopole correction. Weighted angular-mode comparison for $d\ge3$ and a direct matrix comparison for $d=2$ identify the first positive eigenvalue as the unique level-one crossing of an associated spectral radius. The first eigenspace has dimension $d$ in the concentric case and dimension one for every nonconcentric configuration. Convergence and reconstruction estimates justify the coefficient reductions at the two boundaries.
item.dc:creator: Huaian Diao, Jinrui Zhang

item.title: Boundary-layer detachment and infinite-Reynolds limit of two-dimensional wall-bounded flows
item.description: arXiv:2611.15239v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Understanding boundary-layer detachment and its consequences for the infinite-Reynolds-number limit remains a major challenge in fluid mechanics. Here, direct numerical simulations of incompressible flow in a two-dimensional periodic channel with no-slip walls are used to investigate this problem. Reynolds-number-dependent initial conditions are constructed with a boundary layer of Prandtl thickness that converge in the energy norm to an analytic, stationary Euler flow, while the associated Prandtl system develops a finite-time singularity. Highly resolved simulations show boundary-layer detachment and departures from Prandtl scaling, yet provide numerical evidence that the Navier--Stokes solutions continue to converge to the Euler flow over the simulated time interval. In particular, the squared energy norm of the velocity difference and the time-averaged energy dissipation both scale approximately as $Re^{-1/2}$, consistently with established convergence criteria. Although the detached vortices become more numerous and intense as the Reynolds number increases, their characteristic size and occupied area appear to decrease. These observations suggest how boundary-layer detachment and the breakdown of the Prandtl description can coexist with convergence to a smooth Euler flow.
item.dc:creator: Ciro S. Campolina, J\'er\'emie Bec

item.title: Cumulants of Operator Semigroups for Hierarchies of Many-Particle Evolution Equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.15304v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The paper presents a brief overview of recent advances in the mathematical theory of evolution equations for quantum many-particle systems. The structure of expansions representing non-perturbative solutions to the Cauchy problem for hierarchies of fundamental evolution equations for many quantum particles is outlined. It has been shown that the concept of cumulants of operator semigroups forms the basis for non-perturbative representation of solutions to hierarchies of evolution equations that describe the state and observables. It is proven that the constructed dynamics of correlations underlie the description of the evolution of the state, both for finitely and infinitely many particles, governed by the BBGKY hierarchy for reduced density operators or by the hierarchy of nonlinear evolution equations for reduced correlation operators. In fact, it is demonstrated that the behavior of particle correlations governs the dynamics of states in quantum systems with an infinite number of particles.
item.dc:creator: V. I. Gerasimenko

item.title: Weak null singularities for the Einstein--Vlasov system
item.description: arXiv:2611.15318v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the formation and stability of weak null singularities for solutions to the massive and massless Einstein--Vlasov systems without symmetry assumptions. Extending previous results of Luk in the vacuum setting, we establish the existence of spacetimes arising from characteristic initial data that develop a singular null boundary while remaining extendible with a continuous metric. For both massive and massless particles, the energy-momentum tensor and Ricci curvature remain bounded and extend continuously to the singular boundary. For genuinely singular initial data, the Christoffel symbols in the original double-null coordinates fail to be locally square integrable near the boundary. We introduce new commutator vector fields that avoid both derivative loss and the most singular curvature component. Under additional curvature assumptions, we also prove Lipschitz inextendibility across the singular null boundary.
item.dc:creator: Dawei Shen, Yuefeng Song, Jingbo Wan

item.title: Semigroups with periodic complex-time boundedness and holomorphy regions
item.description: arXiv:2611.15455v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the periodicity of complex-time boundedness and holomorphy domains of operator semigroups. We show that an imaginary-time covariance identity involving an isometry yields periodicity of these domains. The method is applied to the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck operator and the hypoelliptic Laplacian on the circle, providing a spectral explanation of periodicity independent of the explicit geometry of their boundedness regions. We also discuss the distinction between boundedness and contractivity, using the classical heat semigroup as an example.
item.dc:creator: M. A. Perelmuter

item.title: Newton's Method and Policy Iterations for Viscous Hamilton--Jacobi Equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.15678v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study Newton's method for the Cauchy problem for viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equations with Hamiltonians that need not be convex. Each Newton step solves a linear parabolic equation obtained by linearizing the equation at the current iterate. We prove that the iterates converge geometrically in \(L^\infty\) from any initial guess satisfying the initial condition, and quadratically in the parabolic H\"older space \(C^{2+\alpha,1+\alpha/2}\) from initial guesses close to the solution. When the Hamiltonian admits a control representation, the Newton iterates coincide with those of classical policy iteration, which therefore inherits both convergence rates. We extend the local quadratic convergence to uniformly parabolic fully nonlinear equations. For small viscosity, we introduce a Nash--Moser variant that smooths the iterate and the residual in space, and we give a convergence criterion with constants independent of the viscosity. Finally, we show how computable residuals certify the error of inexact Newton corrections computed with physics-informed neural networks.
item.dc:creator: Diogo A. Gomes, Xiaoqin Guo, Yeoneung Kim, Hung V. Tran, Yuming P. Zhang

item.title: Point symmetries and Lie reductions of Kadomtsev-Petviashvili equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.15833v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We compute the point symmetry pseudogroup of the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili equation using both the direct and the algebraic methods. We also revisit the classical Lie symmetry analysis of this model in detail, concentrating on hidden infinitesimal and hidden point symmetries. Additionally, we re-examine the symmetry properties of each codimension-one reduced model and determine their point symmetry pseudogroups.
item.dc:creator: Yevhenii Yu. Chapovskyi, Serhii D. Koval

item.title: Gaussian fluctuations and moderate deviations for two-dimensional stochastic nematic liquid crystal flows
item.description: arXiv:2611.15900v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the small-noise behaviour of a two-dimensional stochastic nematic liquid crystal model, where the Navier--Stokes equations with multiplicative noise are coupled with a Ginzburg--Landau equation for the director field driven by geometric Stratonovich noise. While large deviations for stochastic nematic liquid crystal models have been studied earlier, the central limit and moderate deviation regimes have not been considered. We first prove a central limit theorem in the natural energy space and show that the rescaled fluctuations converge, in every $L^p$-norm and with rate $\sqrt{\eps}$, to the solution of a linear stochastic system. The limiting process is centred Gaussian. We then establish a moderate deviation principle with a quadratic rate function determined by the corresponding linearised skeleton equation, which coincides with the Cameron--Martin form of the Gaussian limit. We also show that the moderate deviation principle holds uniformly over bounded sets of initial data. The main arguments use a cancellation between the coupling terms, a one-sided estimate for the polynomial potential, and energy estimates with deterministic Gronwall coefficients, thereby avoiding exponential moment estimates.
item.dc:creator: Akash Ashirbad Panda, Utpal Manna

item.title: On the size of the defect set of an analytic matrix field
item.description: arXiv:2611.16660v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this note, we study the defect set of a symmetric analytic matrix field $M$ defined on an open set $\Omega\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ with $d\ge2$. A defect point $x \in \Omega$ of $M$ is defined as a point for which no eigenframe can be chosen continuously in any neighborhood of $x$. We show that the defect set $S(M)$ is contained in a locally finite union of analytic submanifolds of codimension at least $2$. The proof follows fairly directly from results by Parusinski and Rond (Trans. Am. Math. Soc., 2020) and by Kurdyka and Paunescu (Duke Math. J., 2008). This result can be applied in the context of the Landau-de Gennes Theory to estimate the physical defects of a nematic liquid crystal.
item.dc:creator: Hugo Aubertin

item.title: The uniqueness of smooth stationary black holes
item.description: arXiv:2611.16853v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that the domain of outer communications of a smooth, asymptotically flat, stationary vacuum spacetime describing a single rotating non-degenerate black hole is isometric to the domain of outer communications of a subextremal Kerr solution under reasonable geometric and physical assumptions, without analyticity or any smallness assumptions. The method is to apply Harrison transform to construct a family of solutions of Einstein--Maxwell equations. Combining null area comparison with the area-charge inequality, we show that, in the limiting transformed geometry, the bifurcate sphere has area radius one and constant electric and magnetic flux densities, with the original ADM mass normalized to $M=1$. These identities imply the technical assumptions of Ionescu--Klainerman, yielding the identification with Kerr.
item.dc:creator: Yishen Huang, Jiongyue Li, Junbin Li, Xi-Ping Zhu

item.title: First Order Convergence of Representative Volume Element with Mixed Boundary Condition
