item.description: arXiv:2611.17054v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the cell problem with mixed Dirichlet-Neumann boundary condition to reconstruct the effective matrix for two-dimensional scalar divergence-form equations with bounded measurable, and possibly nonsymmetric coefficients. We prove uniform invertibility of the mean-gradient matrix. Moreover, we derive the first-order error estimate when the medium is periodic.
item.dc:creator: Pingbing Ming, Hao Yu

item.title: Stable $s$-minimal hypersurfaces in dimensions seven and eight
item.description: arXiv:2611.17249v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish optimal sheet separation estimates for stable $s$-minimal hypersurfaces in dimensions up to seven, using an iteration argument in the nonlocal approximation theory of Chan-Dipierro-Serra-Valdinoci. These estimates imply that every stable $s$-minimal hypersurface in $\mathbb{R}^7$ is a hyperplane when $s$ is close to $1$. More generally, every finite Morse index $s$-minimal set in $\mathbb{R}^7$ is a half-space. We also establish a compactness theorem for stable $s$-minimal cones in $\mathbb{R}^8$. We prove uniform curvature and area estimates for their links and show that, as $s \uparrow 1$, they subconverge graphically in $C^{2,\alpha}$, either with multiplicity one to a classical stable minimal cone, or with multiplicity two to a hyperplane. The stability of Lawson and axisymmetric $s$-minimal cones in $\mathbb{R}^8$ shows that these results are optimal.
item.dc:creator: Serena Dipierro, Joaquim Serra, Raphael Tsiamis, Enrico Valdinoci

item.title: Nonrigidity of smooth tight surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.17269v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct smooth isometric embeddings of closed surfaces of positive genus in Euclidean 3-space which are tight, i.e., have minimal total positive curvature, but are not congruent. These embeddings agree outside a compact subset of the region of negative curvature, and enclose different volumes. Thus the rigidity theorem of Alexandrov for analytic tight surfaces does not hold in the smooth category, which settles problems of Nirenberg and Banchoff-Kuhnel.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Ghomi, Hongda Qiu, Matteo Raffaelli, Yuetong Zhang

item.title: Electromagnetic scattering by Minkowski-type bianisotropic media
item.description: arXiv:2311.00584v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the time-harmonic scattering of electromagnetic waves by a bounded stationary inclusion whose effective constitutive law is of Minkowski type. The constant vector $V$ is regarded as a constitutive moving parameter. Such a law arises as an effective description of synthetic moving media and of suitable traveling-wave space--time modulations. Starting from the implicit Minkowski relations, we derive a Maxwell transmission system and its Lippmann--Schwinger volume-integral formulation. The dimensionless parameter $\beta=|V|/c_\Omega$ governs the pointwise constitutive inversion, namely the matrix is invertible precisely for $\beta\neq1$, while on the subcritical branch $0\leq\beta<1$ its inverse admits an explicit convergent expansion. Using the algebraic structure of the cross-product operator, we obtain a spectral characterization of solvability and a quantitative sufficient condition separating the static material contrast from the $V$-dependent contribution which allows to justify the convergence of the corresponding Born series. As an application, we prove that full-aperture electric far-field data at a fixed frequency uniquely determine the support of the inclusion within this perturbative regime without assuming that $V$ is known.
item.dc:creator: Manas Kar, Mourad Sini

item.title: Existence result for a 2 x 2 system of conservation laws with discontinuous flux and applications
item.description: arXiv:2411.12531v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the Cauchy problem for a one-dimensional 2x2 non-symmetric Keyfitz-Kranzer system of conservation laws with a flux f= f(x,U) that is discontinuous with respect to the spatial variable x. No monotonicity assumption is imposed on the mapping x \to f(x,U). We introduce a Kruzhkov-type entropy condition and establish global existence and uniqueness of entropy solutions for initial data with arbitrarily large total variation. The proof relies on a wave-front tracking approximation. The main technical novelty consists in the introduction of adapted Riemann invariant coordinates, specifically designed to account for the discontinuities of the flux, which yield a uniform-in-time bound on the total variation of the approximate solutions U^n(t). As an application, we discuss the second-order ARZ model for vehicular traffic on inhomogeneous roads with abrupt collective changes in the speed law or road capacity.
item.dc:creator: Felisia Angela Chiarello, Simone Fagioli, Massimiliano Daniele Rosini

item.title: Nonlocal elliptic equations involving logarithmic Laplacian: Existence, non-existence and uniqueness results
item.description: arXiv:2411.15985v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, we study the existence, non-existence, and uniqueness results for nonlocal elliptic equations involving logarithmic Laplacian, and subcritical, critical, and supercritical logarithmic nonlinearities. The Poho\u zaev's identity and D\'iaz-Saa type inequality are proved, which are of independent interest and can be applied to a larger class of problems. Depending upon the growth of nonlinearities and regularity of the weight function, we study the small-order asymptotic of nonlocal weighted elliptic equations involving the fractional Laplacian of order $2s.$ We show that the least energy solutions of a weighted nonlocal problem with superlinear or sublinear growth converge to a nontrivial nonnegative least-energy solution of Br\'ezis-Nirenberg type and logistic-type limiting problem respectively involving the logarithmic Laplacian.
item.dc:creator: Rakesh Arora, Jacques Giacomoni, Arshi Vaishnavi

item.title: Boundary value problems for 0-elliptic operators
item.description: arXiv:2412.06084v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $X$ be a manifold with boundary, and let $L$ be a 0-elliptic operator on X which is semi-Fredholm essentially surjective with infinite-dimensional kernel. Examples include Hodge Laplacians and Dirac operators on conformally compact manifolds. We construct left and right parametrices for L when supplemented with appropriate elliptic boundary conditions. The construction relies on a new calculus of pseudodifferential operators on functions over both $X$ and $\partial X$, which we call the "symbolic 0-calculus". This new calculus supplements the ordinary 0-calculus of Mazzeo--Melrose, enabling it to handle boundary value problems. In the original 0-calculus, operators are characterized as polyhomogeneous right densities on a blow-up of $X^2$. By contrast, operators in the symbolic 0-calculus are characterized (locally near each point of the boundary of the diagonal) as quantizations of polyhomogeneous symbols on appropriate blown-up model spaces.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Ars Inveniendi Analytica (2026), Paper No. 4, 153 pp
item.dc:creator: Marco Usula

item.title: Time-optimal problem in the space of probability measures
item.description: arXiv:2502.20871v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper focuses on the value function in the time-optimal problem for a continuity equation in the space of probability measures. We derive the dynamic programming principle for this problem. Using this principle, we prove that the Kruzhkov transform of the value function is a unique discontinuous viscosity solution to the corresponding Dirichlet problem for the Hamilton-Jacobi equation. Finally, we establish the $\Gamma$-convergence of the value function in a perturbed problem to the value function in the unperturbed problem.
item.dc:creator: Yurii Averboukh, Ekaterina Kolpakova

item.title: A convex integration scheme for the continuity equation past the Sobolev embedding threshold
item.description: arXiv:2504.03578v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a convex integration scheme for the continuity equation in the context of the Di Perna-Lions theory that allows to build incompressible vector fields in $C_{t}W^{1,p}_x$ and nonunique solutions in $C_{t} L^{q}_x$ for any $p,q$ with $\frac{1}{p} + \frac{1}{q} > 1 + \frac{1}{d}- \delta$ for some $\delta>0$. This improves the previous bound, corresponding to $\delta=0$, or equivalently $q' > p^*$, obtained with convex integration so far, and critical for those schemes in view of the Sobolev embedding that guarantees that solutions are distributional in the opposite range.
item.dc:creator: Maria Colombo, Roberto Colombo, Anuj Kumar

item.title: A Brezis-Nirenberg Type Problem for a Mixed Local-Nonlocal Operator on the Hyperbolic Space
item.description: arXiv:2505.12936v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper studies nonlinear elliptic equations involving the operator $-\Delta_{\mathbb{B}^N} + (-\Delta_{\mathbb{B}^N})^s-\lambda$ on the hyperbolic space $\mathbb{B}^N$, where $0 < s < 1$ and $\lambda<\frac{(N-1)^2}{4}$. We prove that the best Sobolev constant of this mixed local-nonlocal operator equals the Euclidean Sobolev constant $S$ and is never attained, whereas the corresponding purely local constant may lie strictly below $S$. As a consequence, the purely critical problem has no ground state and no nontrivial solution of small $L^{2^*}$ norm. For the subcritical problem, and for the critical problem with a subcritical perturbation $\mu|u|^{p-1}u$, we obtain nonnegative radial solutions by variational methods, depending on $p$ and $\mu$. Along the way, we prove the continuous embedding $H^1(\mathbb{B}^N)\hookrightarrow H^s(\mathbb{B}^N)$ and the equivalence of the spectral and the pointwise definitions of $(-\Delta_{\mathbb{B}^N})^s$.
item.dc:creator: Diksha Gupta, Konijeti Sreenadh

item.title: Existence of minimizing $n$-harmonic maps in homotopy classes by critical exponents
item.description: arXiv:2506.05060v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the existence of energy minimizing $n$-harmonic maps from an $n$-dimensional sphere to a compact manifold inside a prescribed homotopy class. Our results are of two kinds. First, inspired by the work by T. Rivi\`ere (1998) on minimizing 3-harmonic maps from $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ to $\mathbb{S}^{2}$ with given Hopf degree and by the work of R. Hardt and T. Rivi\`ere (2008) on critical and optimal Sobolev exponents for rational homotopy classes, we exhibit a general principle that guarantees the existence of infinitely many homotopy classes with a minimizing map inside. We apply this principle, each time proving the optimality of the relevant Sobolev exponents, to mappings from $\mathbb{S}^{4n-1}$ to $\mathbb{S}^{2n}$, where the relevant homotopical quantity is the Hopf invariant, and to mappings from $\mathbb{S}^{2n+1}$ to $\mathbb{CP}^{n}$, where homotopy classes are generated by the circle bundle on the projective space. These results hold for first-order as well as for fractional Sobolev mappings. Second, elaborating on the recent preprint of Wang G. and Zhang M. (2026), we derive sharp lower energy bounds for mappings with given Hopf invariant. We apply these bounds to deduce a sufficient energetic condition for the existence of minimizing maps in a given homotopy class. Finally, we exploit this condition, by explicit construction of mappings satisfying it, to prove the existence of energy minimizers from $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ to $\mathbb{S}^{2}$ of Hopf degree $d \in \{\pm2,\pm3,\dotsc,\pm6\}$ and from $\mathbb{S}^{7}$ to $\mathbb{S}^{4}$ of Hopf degree $\pm1$.
item.dc:creator: Antoine Detaille, Adam Grzela, Katarzyna Mazowiecka

item.title: Dissipative solutions for 2D Onsager's conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2506.15396v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 1949, L. Onsager conjectured that weak solutions of the Euler equations in $C_{t,x}^{\gamma}$ are energy conservative when $\gamma>\frac{1}{3}$, whereas nonconservative solutions exist when $\gamma<\frac{1}{3}$. Constantin, E and Titi [13] proved the conservation part, while Isett [26] constructed nontrivial $C^\gamma_{t,x}$ weak solutions with compact support in time in three dimensions for each $0<\gamma<\frac{1}{3}$. Building on this breakthrough work, Buckmaster, De Lellis, Sz\'ekelyhidi Jr. and Vicol [7] obtained strictly dissipative solutions below the Onsager threshold. In two dimensions, Giri and Radu [23] first constructed a nontrivial weak solution in $C^{\frac{1}{3}-}(\mathbb T^2\times[0,T])$ and left an open problem whether it would be possible to construct dissipative solutions (controllable energy) below $\frac{1}{3}$ threshold. In this paper, we reslove this question and thereby obtain infinitely many strictly dissipative weak solutions in $C^\gamma(\mathbb T^2\times[0,T])$ for every $0<\gamma<\frac{1}{3}$. Moreover, we prove that the associated wild initial data are dense in the divergence-free subspace of $C^{\gamma'}(\mathbb{T}^2)$ for any $0<\gamma' <\frac{1}{3}$. The key new ingredient is a family of staircase traveling waves, which we combine with a Picard iteration coupled to the Newton--Nash scheme to control both the Reynolds stress and the kinetic energy. The construction also applies in every dimension $d\geq2$.
item.dc:creator: Lili Du, Xinliang Li, Weikui Ye

item.title: Time asymptotics, time regularity and separation rates for Navier-Stokes flows in supercritical solution classes
item.description: arXiv:2508.00714v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper extends the weak solution theory for the 3D Navier-Stokes equations of Barker, Seregin and Sverak from a critical setting to a supercritical setting making sure to include a useful a priori energy bound as well as a statement about stability under weak-star convergence. Two applications of the a priori bound are then explored. The first provides a spatially local, short-time asymptotic expansion in the time variable starting at $t=0$ which, as a corollary, provides an upper bound on how fast hypothetical non-unique solutions to the Navier-Stokes equations can separate locally. The second establishes higher-order time regularity at a singular time and at spatial points positioned away from the singularity. This quantifies the degree to which the non-local nature of the pressure allows a far flung singularity to disrupt the time regularity at a regular point.
item.dc:creator: Zachary Bradshaw, Joshua Hudson

item.title: Bounds for spectral projectors on the three-dimensional torus
item.description: arXiv:2508.05573v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study $L^2$ to $L^p$ operator norms of spectral projectors for the Euclidean Laplacian on the torus in the case where the spectral window is narrow. With a window of constant size this is a classical result of Sogge; in the small-window limit we are left with $L^p$ norms of eigenfunctions of the Laplacian, as considered for instance by Bourgain. For the three-dimensional torus we prove new cases of a previous conjecture of the first two authors concerning the size of these norms; we also refine certain prior results to remove $\epsilon$-losses in all dimensions. We use methods from number theory: the geometry of numbers, the circle method and exponential sum bounds due to Guo. We complement these techniques with height splitting and a bilinear argument to prove sharp results. We exposit on the various techniques used and their limitations.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Ars Inveniendi Analytica (2026), Paper No. 6, 49 pp
item.dc:creator: Pierre Germain, Simon L. Rydin Myerson, Daniel Pezzi

item.title: On a fractional Alt-Caffarelli-Friedman-type monotonicity formula
item.description: arXiv:2509.25891v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, by exploiting mean value properties of $s$-harmonic functions, we introduce some monotonicity formulas in the nonlocal setting. Our approach is purely nonlocal and does not rely on the extension technique. As a byproduct we also establish interior nonlocal gradient estimates and a nonlocal analogue of the Bochner identity.
item.dc:creator: Fausto Ferrari, Davide Giovagnoli, Enzo Maria Merlino

item.title: Polychromatic Localized Waves with Complex Frequencies in Nonlinear Maxwell Equations with Material Dispersion
item.description: arXiv:2511.21467v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the existence of polychromatic solutions of cubically nonlinear Maxwell equations in the whole space and with dispersive media, i.e., with a time delayed polarization. Due to the complex nature of the dielectric function, the frequencies are complex, resulting in a decay in time. The geometry is that of a waveguide in $x$ with the propagation direction being $y$ and the solutions are localized in $x$ and have a transverse magnetic polarization. These are often referred to as breathers. They are given as a Fourier series in $y$ and $t$ with the leading frequency $\omega$ being an eigenvalue of a corresponding operator pencil on $\mathbb{R}$ (in the $x$ variable). Each term in the series corresponds to a different temporal decay rate or a different frequency. The series is constructed iteratively via a sequence of linear ordinary differential equations. Our general result provides the existence under some assumptions on the spectrum and on estimates of the resolvent of the corresponding linear operator. We also produce an example of a waveguide given by the interface of two spatially homogeneous physically relevant media for which these assumptions are satisfied. For such an interface setting the constructed solutions correspond to nonlinear polychromatic surface plasmons.
item.dc:creator: Tomas Dohnal, Maximilian Hanisch, Runan He

item.title: On the well-posedness of two-dimensional Hele-Shaw flow with an elastic interface
item.description: arXiv:2601.01374v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate a two-dimensional Hele-Shaw free-boundary problem with a nonlinear elastic interface, for both one-phase and two-phase scenarios. Using the paradifferential formulation, we demonstrate that the problem is locally well-posed in $H^s$ for $s\geq 2$ for arbitrary initial data. Furthermore, for the one-phase case and the stable two-phase case $(\rho^+ \leq \rho^-)$, we establish global well-posedness for small initial data in $H^s$ when $s> \frac{3}{2}$.
item.dc:creator: Lizhe Wan, Jiaqi Yang

item.title: Convergence analysis of a semi-implicit time discretization for the doubly degenerate Richards equation
item.description: arXiv:2602.19037v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A key contribution of this work is the derivation of convergence results for the semi-implicit time discretization in the general doubly degenerate setting. This paper presents a mathematical analysis of a doubly degenerate parabolic equation and its application to the Richards equation using a bounded auxiliary variable. We establish the existence of weak solutions using a semi-implicit time discretization combined with maximal monotone operator theory. The analysis is conducted within weighted Sobolev spaces, allowing for a rigorous treatment of the equation's strict degeneracy and strong nonlinearities. Unlike previous works that often rely on strict parabolicity or high regularity, we establish these results without imposing strictly positive lower bounds on the diffusivity. Furthermore, we prove that the Richards equation using the introduced auxiliary variable preserves the physical bounds of the saturation and demonstrate the unconditional linear convergence of the L-scheme linearization to the semi-discrete solution.
item.dc:creator: Abderrahmane Benfanich, Yves Bourgault, Abdelaziz Beljadid

item.title: Duality for the Adversarial Total Variation
item.description: arXiv:2604.18540v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Adversarial training of binary classifiers can be reformulated as regularized risk minimization involving a nonlocal total variation. Building on this perspective, we establish a characterization of the subdifferential of this total variation using duality techniques. To achieve this, we derive a dual representation of the nonlocal total variation and a related integration-by-parts formula, involving a nonlocal gradient and divergence. We provide such duality statements both in the space of continuous functions vanishing at infinity on proper metric spaces and for the space of essentially bounded functions on separable metric spaces. Furthermore, under some additional conditions we provide characterizations of the subdifferential in these settings.
item.dc:creator: Leon Bungert, Lucas Schmitt

item.title: Bilinear embedding for divergence-form operators with first-order terms and negative potentials
item.description: arXiv:2605.14699v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This article establishes a bilinear embedding for second-order divergence-form operators with complex coefficients, characterized by the simultaneous presence of first-order terms and negative potentials. This work provides a further development of the theory initiated by Carbonaro and Dragi\v{c}evi\'c for the homogeneous case, and recently extended by the second author in two papers where first-order terms and negative potentials were treated separately. We work in the general setting of arbitrary open subsets of $\mathbb{R}^d$ under Dirichlet, Neumann, or mixed boundary conditions. Our main contribution is the introduction of a unified notion of generalized $p$-ellipticity that extends all its predecessors and serves as the natural condition for the bilinear inequality. Methodologically, we overcome the rigidity of the Bellman-heat method on arbitrary open subsets by introducing a novel sequence-based approach that unifies and simplifies the previous techniques. As fundamental applications, we prove the boundedness of the $H^\infty$-calculus on $L^p$ and establish $L^p$-maximal regularity. Moreover, we show that this generalized $p$-ellipticity provides a sufficient condition for the $L^p$-contractivity and $L^p$-analyticity of the generated semigroup. Finally, we apply our theory to magnetic Schr\"odinger operators, characterizing the range of exponents $p$ for which the associated coefficient tuple satisfies the generalized $p$-ellipticity condition introduced here.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Luciano Morelato, Andrea Poggio

item.title: Refined asymptotic estimates, Morse index and nondegeneracy of solutions to a biharmonic problem with large exponents in dimension four

item.dc:creator: Xiuda Liang, Wangwang Peng, Shuying Tian, Wenjie Wang

item.title: Higher integrability for parabolic double phase equations with an improved gap bound
item.description: arXiv:2606.10590v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a local higher integrability result for the gradient of \textit{a priori} H\"older continuous weak solutions to the parabolic double phase equation \[ \partial_t u - \operatorname{div} \left(|Du|^{p-2}Du + a(z)|Du|^{q-2}Du\right) = 0 \qquad \text{in } \Omega_T. \] We work under a relaxed gap condition on the exponents $p$ and $q$. The coefficient $a$ is assumed to belong to the class $\mathcal{Z}^{\kappa}(\Omega_T)$ for some $\kappa \in (0,\infty)$. The functions in this class satisfy a one-sided pointwise bound that controls how fast $a$ can grow away from its zero set, and the class contains the H\"older continuous functions. We also impose a \emph{mild almost increasing} condition on $a$, which motivates the introduction of a new mollification, which we call the \emph{slanted Steklov average}. For $u \in C^{0,\gamma,\gamma/q}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega_T)$ with $\gamma \in [0,1)$, our main result holds under the gap bound \begin{equation}\tag{G}\label{eq:G} 2 \le p \le q, \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, (q-p)(q-2\gamma)\leq q\kappa \end{equation} The new gap condition \eqref{eq:G} is purely parabolic in nature and is stricter than the optimal gap relation associated with the Lavrentiev phenomenon for the elliptic double phase functional.
item.dc:creator: Abhrojyoti Sen, Jarkko Siltakoski

item.title: Global existence, blow-up behavior and numerical simulations for a class of chemotaxis-driven fish-mussel systems
item.description: arXiv:2606.18695v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, we investigate a chemotaxis-driven fish--mussel ecosystem model described by a coupled system of partial differential equations subject to homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions. Under suitable assumptions on the system parameters and initial data, we establish the global existence of classical solutions by employing semigroup methods together with a priori estimates. We also examine the possible blow-up behavior of solutions in a three-dimensional domain. To support the theoretical analysis, a finite element method is developed for the numerical approximation of the system, and convergence studies based on mesh refinement are carried out to verify the accuracy and stability of the proposed numerical scheme. Furthermore, numerical simulations illustrating the blow-up behavior of solutions in the computational domain are presented.
item.dc:creator: Gnanasekaran Shanmugasundaram, Jitraj Saha

item.title: Remarks on some quasi-linear fourth order parabolic equations arising in mathematical physics
item.description: arXiv:2607.27451v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This note proves existence and uniqueness of strong solutions to a broad class of fourth-order quasi-linear parabolic equations in the class of Wiener spaces. It improves upon previous results in the literature, devoted to some special cases falling within the general framework developed here, in which uniqueness held true in a smaller class than the space where existence was proven. Gain of analyticity, as well as generalisations to higher-order equations and to propagation of higher regularities, are also discussed.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Fanelli, Rafael Granero-Belinch\'on, Martina Magliocca, Matthieu Pageard

item.title: Small-data $L^2$ theory for the intermediate NLS and the Calogero--Moser derivative NLS
item.description: arXiv:2608.01138v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study a class of nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations (NLS) in a unified way. This class includes two important examples: the intermediate NLS (INLS) and the Calogero--Moser derivative NLS (CM-DNLS). Our main results are twofold. First, we prove small-data global well-posedness in $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ for a broad class of equations. This includes both focusing and defocusing CM-DNLS and the INLS for arbitrary choices of its parameters. Second, we prove small-data scattering in $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ under an additional assumption. This result covers both focusing and defocusing CM-DNLS and the INLS for specific choices of its parameters. Both the formulation of the problem, including the notion of solution, and the proofs rely crucially on a linear theory for Schr\"odinger equations with rough time-dependent potentials. This theory is also of independent interest, since we allow potentials so rough that the standard Duhamel formulation may not make sense. Our approach is perturbative and is built on the bilinear Strichartz estimate proved by Ozawa and Tsutsumi in 1998. In particular, our argument does not rely on integrability.
item.dc:creator: Sonae Hadama

item.title: Poisson problem with Hardy operator on lattice graph $ \mathbb{Z}^d$ and the application to semilinear equations
item.description: arXiv:2609.13933v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the analytic properties of the Hardy-type operator $-\Delta + \mu H_0$ on the $d$-dimensional integer lattice graph $\mathbb{Z}^d$, where $\mu \geq -1$ and $H_0$ is a critical Hardy potential at infinity--arising naturally from discrete Hardy inequalities. We derive sharp fixed-pole Green kernel estimates on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ and obtain a necessary and sufficient weighted summability condition characterizing the solvability of the nonnegative Poisson problem associated with this operator. Building upon this classification, we provide a complete characterization of the nonexistence of positive solutions to the semilinear elliptic inequality $$ -\Delta u + \mu H_0 u \geq W u^p \quad \text{in } \mathbb{Z}^d, $$ where $p > 0$, $d \geq 3$, $\mu \geq -1$, and $H_0, W \in C(\mathbb{Z}^d)$ are strictly positive potentials satisfying the asymptotic behaviors $H_0(x) \sim |x|^{-2}$ and $W(x) \sim |x|^{\theta}$ as $|x| \to \infty$, with $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$.
item.dc:creator: Huyuan Chen, Bobo Hua, Wendi Xu

item.title: Sufficient conditions for multiplicity and uniqueness of positive solutions of the H\'enon equation
item.description: arXiv:2609.18039v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish explicit sufficient conditions for multiplicity of positive solutions of the H\'enon equation in the unit ball and for uniqueness in one dimension. In the Sobolev-subcritical range, a spherical harmonic function argument shows that the radial solution has Morse index greater than one and therefore differs from a ground state. In even dimensions, a degree-four perturbation in a symmetry and monotonicity cone yields a sufficient condition for nonradiality in the supercritical range. The one-dimensional uniqueness criterion follows from a comparison of weighted Dirichlet eigenvalues and a concavity estimate.
item.dc:creator: Geyang Du

item.title: The $m$-Laplace equation with a gradient term I: Liouville theorem in the second subcritical case
item.description: arXiv:2609.30006v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $1<m<n$, $q>0$, and $p\in\mathbb R$. We study positive $C^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ weak solutions of \[-\Delta_m u=u^p|Du|^q\qquad\text{in }\mathbb R^n.\] If $0<q<m-1$, we prove that every such solution is constant provided \[p+q-m+1<\frac{(m-1)(m-q)^2}{(n-m)(m-1-q)}.\] If $q\geqslant m-1$, the same conclusion holds for every $p\in\mathbb R$. For $0<q<m$, the proof uses an auxiliary function and reduces the main differential estimate to a lower bound for a function of one variable. An explicit construction and a local maximum-principle argument then prove constancy without differentiating across $\{|Du|=0\}$. When $m=2$, our result answers the natural Liouville problem left open by Bidaut-V\'eron, Garc\'ia-Huidobro and V\'eron for the whole range $0<q<1$. The case $q\geqslant m$ is handled by the related work of Bidaut-V\'eron.
item.dc:creator: Tian Wu, Jin Yan, Hua Zhu

item.title: A Spacetime-Diffeomorphic Approach to Magnetohydrodynamics around Black Holes: Dilation Covariance, Linearization,and the No-Hair Limit
item.description: arXiv:2610.04983v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The ideal magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) system that governs a conducting plasma---the Maxwell equations together with the conservation laws of mass, momentum and energy---is the same local balance structure that describes hot accretion flows around black holes. We introduce a uniform four-dimensional spacetime dilation \[ \Phi_L:\;(t',x',y',z')\mapsto (t,x,y,z)=(Lt',Lx',Ly',Lz'),\qquad L>1, \] and show that it is a smooth, orientation-preserving $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism of flat spacetime. Pulling the MHD conservation laws back through $\Phi_L$, we prove that the closed ideal-MHD system is form-invariant (covariant), with the current density rescaling as $\bm j=\bm j'/L$, the magnetic diffusivity as $\eta'=\eta/L$, and external sources rescaled by $L$. The transformation realises three physically distinct effects on the perturbed flow: a \emph{linearization} to the tangent-space (linearised MHD) system, a \emph{movie slow-motion} dilation of dissipative and dynamical timescales, and an \emph{electron-microscope} magnification of small-scale structure. Taking the formal limit $L\to\infty$ localises the dynamics on a neighbourhood of a horizon: resistivity vanishes, the asymptotic time derivative freezes, and all transient multipolar structure of the infalling plasma redshifts away. The remaining stationary, axisymmetric, asymptotically flat electrovacuum is uniquely the Kerr--Newman geometry, so that the exterior of the compact object is characterised only by its mass $M$, angular momentum $J$ and charge $Q$. The result provides a local, conservation-law-based perspective on the black hole no-hair theorem that is complementary to the classical Israel--Carter-- Robinson theorems and to contemporary gravitational-wave and Event Horizon Telescope tests.
item.dc:creator: Yuanya Li

item.title: A Circular Cantor Construction Without Dimension Drop for Harmonic Measure
item.description: arXiv:2610.15759v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For every $0<s<1$ we construct a compact $s$-Ahlfors regular set $K\subset\mathbb C$ for which harmonic measure of $\mathbb C\setminus K$ with pole at infinity is comparable to $\mathcal H^s|_K$. In particular, there is no dimension drop for harmonic measure in the domain $\mathbb C\setminus K$. The construction is $N$-adic and based on configurations close to the $N$-th roots of unity. Our construction with corrections to the first order gives the range $0<s<2/3$, while corrections of arbitrary finite order yield the full range $0<s<1$.
item.dc:creator: Yingying Cai, Cole Jeznach, Xavier Tolsa

item.title: Spectral stability for strong ideal-gas shock layers
item.description: arXiv:2610.22660v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a purely analytical proof of one-dimensional spectral stability of sufficiently strong shock layers for the full ideal-gas Navier--Stokes equations with constant viscosity and heat conduction. Earlier work reduced this question to a limiting problem and gave strong numerical evidence of stability through Evans function computation, but no proof. We prove stability for every adiabatic index $1<\gamma<3$ and for an explicit range of ratios of heat conduction to viscosity that contains all common gases.
item.dc:creator: Jeffrey Humpherys

item.title: Global regularity and sharp decay rates for the one-dimensional hypo-viscous compressible Navier-Stokes equations in critical Besov spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.25889v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study the global regularity for the one-dimensional hypo-viscous compressible Navier-Stokes equations in the critical Besov spaces, where the initial data are close to the constant equilibrium state. We introduce an effective velocity, constructed as a combination of the density and the velocity, which is used to capture the high-frequency behavior of $a$. By performing elaborate high-frequency and low-frequency estimates together with a bootstrap argument, we obtain global existence for $\frac{1}{2}\le\beta<1$. In particular, when $\beta=\frac{1}{2}$, we also prove the system is well-posed in critical space. Furthermore, under an additional low-frequency assumption, we establish the optimal time decay rates.
item.dc:creator: Chen Liang, Zhaonan Luo, Zhaoyang Yin

item.title: Improved Sobolev and Moser--Trudinger--Onofri Inequalities under Constraints: Sharpness and Quantitative Remainders
item.description: arXiv:2610.26691v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study improved Sobolev and Moser--Trudinger--Onofri inequalities on the sphere under moment constraints, with particular emphasis on sharp leading constants and quantitative remainder terms. For the Sobolev inequality, we sharpen the almost sharp inequality of Hang and Wang [30] (Int. Math. Res. Not., 2022) to a sharp one at $p=2$ under vanishing moment constraints of orders $m=1,2,3$. We also prove a general failure principle: if the unconstrained sharp Sobolev inequality fails, then the corresponding sharp improved inequality under moment constraints fails as well. For the Moser--Trudinger--Onofri inequality, we sharpen the almost sharp inequalities of Chang and Hang [10] and Hang [29] (Comm. Pure Appl. Math., 2022) to a sharp improved inequality at the critical order $s=\frac{n}{2}$ under arbitrary finite-order moment constraints. We further investigate the best remainder constant. In contrast with the two-dimensional first-moment case of Gui and Moradifam [28] (Invent. Math., 2018), where the best remainder vanishes, we show that it is positive in several higher-dimensional regimes. We also obtain quantitative remainder estimates for general almost sharp improved Sobolev and Moser--Trudinger--Onofri inequalities, which in turn yield sharp inequalities at different scales. We further extend recent second-moment refinements to higher dimensions and higher orders. Finally, we obtain analogous results on sharpness, non-sharpness, and quantitative remainder estimates for improved Sobolev-type inequalities under symmetry constraints on general smooth closed manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Yuxuan Zhou, Wenming Zou

item.title: Sharp Defect Thresholds and Concentration for Radial Elliptic Equations and Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.31167v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we consider positive radial entire solutions of nonlinear elliptic equations with bounded positive coefficients and optimize the negative logarithmic derivative of the coefficient. For the scalar equation, we determine the exact, unattained defect threshold and establish quantitative gaps when the coefficient ratio is fixed. Near the threshold, we prove a sharp stability estimate and describe the loss of compactness through a profile decomposition in logarithmic radius, including a characterization of the possible diffuse energy and conditions that exclude it. We also show that the resulting profile configurations can be realized by suitable monotone coefficients. For unequal weighted elliptic systems, we obtain the corresponding sharp defect threshold and fixed-ratio gap, and analyze near-threshold sequences through local homogeneous limits and logarithmic spreading. A BV relaxation and smoothing argument further relates the relaxed and smooth optimization problems.
item.dc:creator: Shengbing Deng, Bo Zhang

item.title: Corner Regularity and Asymptotics for the Two-Dimensional Radiation Transport Equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.32732v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The regularity of solutions to the two-dimensional radiation transport equation plays a central role in understanding the behavior of scalar flux near geometric corners. In a previous study of Kaper's corner singularity problem, the physical transport kernel was decomposed into its principal inverse-distance singularity and a lower-order remainder, reducing the corner asymptotic analysis to the question of whether the scalar flux possesses sufficient continuity to justify differentiation of the associated singular potential. The required regularity, however, remained unresolved. In this paper, we establish a sharp modulus-of-continuity estimate for the scalar flux generated by the physical transport kernel and prove the estimate $\omega_{\phi}(h)=O\!\left(h\log(D/h)\right)$, which implies Dini continuity. This estimate yields absolute convergence of the fluctuation term arising in the differentiated principal potential and permits a rigorous differentiation formula for transport solutions. Using this regularity framework, we derive the fixed-angle asymptotic behavior of the scalar flux and its first derivatives near a rectangular corner. For every fixed interior ray, the gradient exhibits logarithmic growth, while the scalar flux admits an $r\log(1/r)$ correction with an explicitly identified coefficient determined by the corner values of the flux and source. The analysis shows that a rectangular corner does not generate a singularity stronger than the logarithmic first-derivative singularity already present in smooth-boundary transport theory. Numerical calculations on benchmark problems are consistent with the theoretical predictions. These results provide a rigorous resolution of the regularity issue underlying Kaper's corner singularity problem and establish a mathematical framework for corner asymptotics in two-dimensional radiation transport.
item.dc:creator: Dean Wang

item.title: Long-time action stability for perturbed KdV near finite-gap tori
item.description: arXiv:2610.34601v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove action and spectral stability near finite-gap tori of the periodic Korteweg--de Vries equation under autonomous analytic Hamiltonian perturbations of size $\varepsilon$. The estimates are uniform over prescribed compact families, without small-amplitude or nonresonance assumptions, and allow nearby initial data with infinitely many open gaps. Assuming a strong solution and a uniform higher Sobolev bound on $[0,T_0/\varepsilon]$, we permit one-derivative loss in the perturbing Hamiltonian's normal gradient. For sufficiently small $\varepsilon$ and initial normal Birkhoff size $r_0$, the tangential action variations and weighted sum of normal actions are bounded by $C_\delta(r_0^2+\varepsilon^{2\delta})$, while the spectral-gap variation in $\ell^2$ is bounded by $C_\delta(r_0+\varepsilon^\delta)$, for every $0<\delta<1/4$. A key ingredient is coercivity of the negative Hessian of the nonlinear KdV Hamiltonian on the full $\ell^2$ action space at every finite-gap action. We combine this with resonance analysis and corrected action observables evaluated along the solution. The hypotheses are verified for several local and nonlocal Hamiltonian perturbations.
item.dc:creator: Guan Huang

item.title: Regularization and Full Support for the CBO Equation with Measure Initial Data
item.description: arXiv:2610.35266v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove global well-posedness and regularization for the isotropic consensus-based optimization equation with initial probability measures of finite fourth moment. Under suitable weight decay assumptions, after any nonconstant consensus motion, both the density and the consensus trajectory become smooth, and all spatial Sobolev norms are locally bounded in time. The proof uses a Fourier commutator estimate, localization and iteration, followed by a nonlinear time bootstrap. Counterexamples show that smoothing can fail at a stationary consensus point. For non-Dirac initial data, we also prove positivity away from the consensus point and full support at every positive time in all dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Lukang Sun

item.title: Linearize or Discretize First? Error Estimates under Mesh-Uniform Regularity and Exponential Stability for the KdV Equation with Boundary Dissipation
item.description: arXiv:2610.39269v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the Korteweg-de Vries equation on a bounded interval with boundary dissipation, and its spatial semidiscretization by a weighted cubic Hermite Galerkin method. A small nonlinear wave can be approximated by a linear discrete simulation in two orders: linearize first and then discretize, or discretize first and then linearize. Both orders lead to the same total error. They divide this error differently between linearization and discretization. The difference of the two divisions is what we call the ordering error. We show that it is quadratic in the size of the initial datum and carries a positive power of the mesh size, for all time. It can be used to assess the effect of a coarse-mesh correction for nonlinear problems. For the continuous problem, the solution map is analytic, and the semigroup of the linearized equation has Crandall-Pazy regularity with the exact index 3/2. For the weighted scheme, the discrete semigroups of the linearized equation inherit exponential stability, Kato smoothing and Crandall-Pazy regularity, with bounds uniform in the mesh size. The nonlinear solution maps are analytic, also uniformly in the mesh size. These properties give error estimates in which the error and the datum are measured in the same norm: in the energy norm, in $H_0^1$ and in $H^2$. On every interval $[t_0,\infty)$, $t_0>0$, same-norm convergence holds uniformly on balls at algebraic rates. The ordering error is of order $h^{1/6}$ times the square of the energy norm of the datum, uniformly for all $t\ge0$.
item.dc:creator: Kangsheng Liu

item.title: A sharp lower bound for torsional rigidity of convex domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.39666v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For every bounded convex domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, we establish the following sharp inequality for torsional rigidity $$\frac{2(d+1)}{d}\int\limits_\Omega\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial\Omega)^2{\,\mathrm d} x\le T(\Omega),$$ where $T(\Omega)=4\int\limits_\Omega u{\,\mathrm d} x$ and $-\Delta u=1$ in $\Omega$, $u\in H_0^1(\Omega)$. Moreover, equality holds if and only if $\Omega$ is a ball.
item.dc:creator: M. A. Perelmuter

item.title: Effective threshold dynamics for the cubic nonlinear Klein-Gordon equation in three dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.41718v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the focussing cubic Klein-Gordon equation on $\mathbb{R}^{3+1}$ in the radial setting. Foundational work by Nakanishi-Schlag gives a complete qualitative characterisation of the dynamics near the ground state $Q$, in particular revealing a threshold phenomenon, whereby a co-dimension one Lipschitz manifold separates finite time blow up from scattering solutions in forward time. Our aim in this paper is to derive an effective bound for the scattering norm $\|u\|_{L_t^3([0,\infty);L_x^6(\mathbb{R}^3))}$, for scattering energy class solutions $u$ with data sufficiently near $Q$ and close to the threshold manifold. This requires the development of an induction on energy strategy in a setting where an alternative to the usual Morawetz approach appears necessary.
item.dc:creator: Jaime G\'omez, Joachim Krieger

item.title: Stable solutions to $p$-Laplacian type equations with variable coefficients
item.description:
arXiv:2611.00730v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study stable regular solutions of the equation $-\operatorname{div} igg(\Big(A(x)
abla u \cdot 
abla u\Big)^{p/2-1}A(x)
abla u igg) = f(u)$ in $B_1 \subset \mathbb{R}^n$, where $p > 1$, $f \in C^1(\mathbb{R})$ is nonnegative, and $A$ is a locally Lipschitz, symmetric, uniformly elliptic matrix field. We prove that stable regular solutions satisfy an interior H"older estimate for $n < p + 4p/(p - 1)$ when $p \ge 2$, and for $n < 5p$ when $1 < p < 2$. This extends the result of Cabr'e, Miraglio, and Sanch'on [7] for the $p$-Laplace equation. Note that the constant in our H"older estimate depends on the local $C^1$ norm of $A$, but not on its $C^2$ norm. Our approach is motivated by the interior regularity estimates of Cabr'e, Miraglio, and Sanch'on [7] for the $p$-Laplace equation and by Erneta's [14] treatment of variable coefficients in semilinear elliptic equations.
item.dc:creator: Weican Luo

item.title: Sharp asymptotic stability of the IPM equation in $\mathbb{R}^2$ via isopycnal coordinates
item.description: arXiv:2611.06241v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the incompressible porous media (IPM) equation, a model describing the motion of a fluid with variable density through a porous medium under the action of gravity. We prove that the stably stratified state, in which heavier fluid lies below lighter fluid, is nonlinearly stable: small perturbations decay over time and the fluid returns to equilibrium. Our result holds in the sharp Sobolev setting $H^s(\mathbb R^2)$ for every $s>2$: this threshold cannot be improved, since the equation is ill-posed in $H^2(\mathbb R^2)$. This result follows from a proof of global well-posedness at critical Besov regularity, with smallness required only in a norm invariant under the natural scaling of the equation. We also prove optimal decay rates for suitably localized initial data. The main difficulty is that the stabilizing effect of stratification acts only in some directions, while the nonlinear transport acts in all of them. Reaching the sharp regularity threshold requires two main novelties. First, we rewrite the equation in \emph{isopycnal coordinates}, which follow the level sets of the density: in these coordinates the transport becomes one-dimensional, and the anisotropic stabilizing mechanism can be exploited at minimal regularity. Second, we establish new \emph{anisotropic commutator estimates} which allow us to control the remaining nonlinear terms. Finally, we show that the estimates obtained in isopycnal coordinates can be transferred back to the original variables.
item.dc:creator: Roberta Bianchini, Timoth\'ee Crin-Barat, Ling-Yun Shou, Shan Wang

item.title: Large-Time Behavior and Asymptotic Profiles for Time-Fractional Nonlinear Diffusion Equations via Entropy Methods
item.description: arXiv:2611.09858v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the large-time behavior of nonnegative solutions to the time-fractional nonlinear diffusion equation $\partial_t^{\alpha}(u-u_0) = \Delta u^m$, $0<\alpha<1$, $m>0$, in a bounded domain with the homogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition. We prove that the rescaled solution $t^{\frac{\alpha}{m}}u$ converges as $t\to\infty$ to an asymptotic profile $S$ characterized by $-\Delta S^m = u_0/\Gamma(1-\alpha)$. Moreover, we show that $t^\alpha u^m$ converges to $S^m$, which admits an explicit representation in terms of the Green function and the initial datum. In contrast to the classical case $\alpha=1$, the asymptotic profile depends explicitly on the initial datum.
item.dc:creator: Mikiya Kametaka

item.title: On the Abels--Garcke--Gr\"un Model for Incompressible Two-Phase Flows with Unmatched Densities: Phase Separation and Rayleigh--Taylor Instability
item.description: arXiv:2611.12298v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Instability phenomena are ubiquitous in multi-fluid flows. For binary fluid mixtures, phase separation may occur under specific conditions, in which a homogeneous state becomes unstable and spontaneously segregates into different phases, leading to the formation of distinct patterns. Furthermore, when a heavier fluid is superposed over a lighter one in a gravitational field, the fluid interface can be sensitive to perturbations that trigger the Rayleigh--Taylor (RT) instability, i.e., the lighter fluid penetrates upward into the heavier fluid against gravity. We investigate such instability phenomena and the inhibiting conditions for incompressible, immiscible two-phase flows with unmatched densities, within the framework of a diffuse-interface model, which is called the Abels--Garcke--Gr\"un (AGG) model. More precisely, we adopt energy methods to establish several stability/instability conditions for the perturbed system of the AGG model, which is obtained by slightly perturbing the equilibrium profile $(\mathbf{0},\overline{\varphi})$, where $\overline{\varphi}=\overline{\varphi}(x_3)$ depends solely on the vertical coordinate $x_3$. Notably, for a constant equilibrium profile $\overline{\varphi}=\alpha\in(-1,1)$ satisfying $\Psi''(\alpha)<0$, we establish a threshold for stability and instability of the phase-separation problem. Similar stability results are also established for the perturbed system with $\overline{\varphi}$ satisfying the RT instability condition in the presence of gravity. In particular, if the phase-separation condition fails and $\partial_{x_3}\overline{\varphi}$ is a constant, a larger value of $\partial_{x_3}\overline{\varphi}$, a greater interfacial thickness and a higher surface energy density contribute to inhibiting RT instability.
item.dc:creator: Fei Jiang, Maoyin Lv, Hao Wu

item.title: An almost sharp $L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{d})$-$L^{2}(\mathbb{S}^{d-1})$ restriction theorem for a class of anisotropic operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.12463v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $d\geq 2$. For each $j\in \{1,\dots,d\}$, let ${\ell}_{j}\geq 1$ and $m_{j}\geq 2$ be integers, and let $a_{j}$ be a nonzero real number. We prove that the oscillatory integral operator \begin{equation*} T_{{\ell}_{1},\dots,{\ell}_{d},m_{1},\dots,m_{d}}f(x):=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}} e^{\dot{\imath} \left(a_{1}x^{{\ell}_{1}}_{1}y^{m_{1}}_{1}+\dots +a_{d}x^{{\ell}_{d}}_{d}y^{m_{d}}_{d} \right)}f(y)dy,\;\;\; x\in \mathbb{R}^{d}, \end{equation*} satisfies the restriction estimate \begin{equation*} \|T_{{\ell}_{1},\dots,{\ell}_{d},m_{1},\dots,m_{d}} f\|_{L^{2}(\mathbb{S}^{d-1})}\lesssim \|f\|_{L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{d})}, \end{equation*} whenever \begin{equation*} \mathcal{U}:= \min{\left\{ \min_{1\leq j\leq d}{\frac{m_{j}}{{\ell}_{j}}},\,\min_{1\leq k\leq d}{\frac{d-1}{\sum_{j\neq k} \frac{\ell_{j}}{m_{j}}+\frac{2}{m_{k}}}}\right\}}>1, \end{equation*} and we necessarily have $\mathcal{U}\geq 1$.
item.dc:creator: Ahmed A. Abdelhakim

item.title: Parabolic stochastic quantisation of the fractional $\Phi^4_3$ model in the full subcritical regime
item.description: arXiv:2303.18112v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a construction of the measure of the fractional $\Phi^4$ Euclidean quantum field theory on $\mathbb{R}^3$ in the full subcritical regime via parabolic stochastic quantisation. Our approach is based on a truncated flow equation for the effective description of the model at sufficiently small scales and on coercive estimates for the nonlinear stochastic partial differential equation describing the interacting field. The constructed measure is translation invariant, reflection positive, and has quartic exponential tails.
item.dc:creator: Pawe{\l} Duch, Massimiliano Gubinelli, Paolo Rinaldi

item.title: Optimizing the ground state energy of the three-dimensional magnetic Dirichlet Laplacian with constant magnetic field
item.description: arXiv:2504.21597v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper concerns the shape optimization problem of minimizing the ground state energy of the magnetic Dirichlet Laplacian with constant magnetic field among three-dimensional domains of fixed volume. In contrast to the two-dimensional case, a generalized "magnetic" Faber-Krahn inequality does not hold and minimizers cannot be balls when the magnetic field is turned on. An analysis of the problem among cylindrical domains reveals geometric constraints for general minimizers. In particular, minimizers must elongate with a certain rate along the direction of the magnetic field as the field strength increases. In addition to the theoretical analysis, we present numerical minimizers which confirm this prediction and give rise to further conjectures.
item.dc:creator: Matthias Baur

item.title: A PINNs approach for the computation of eigenvalues in elliptic problems
item.description: arXiv:2507.03126v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we propose a method for computing eigenvalues of elliptic problems using Deep Learning techniques. A key feature of our approach is that it is independent of the space dimension and can compute arbitrary eigenvalues without requiring the prior computation of lower ones. Moreover, the method can be easily adapted to handle nonlinear eigenvalue problems.
item.dc:creator: Julian Fernandez Bonder, Ariel M. Salort

item.title: Spectral gaps and uniqueness in the isotropic $L_p$ Minkowski problem
item.description: arXiv:2509.08588v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the isotropic $L_p$ Minkowski problem in $\mathbb{R}^n$ for $p<-n$. We prove that a smooth strictly convex solution $K$ is the unit ball if the second non-zero eigenvalue of the Hilbert-Brunn-Minkowski operator satisfies $\lambda_2(-L_K)\ge\frac{-p-1}{n-1}$. We also derive a lower bound for $\lambda_2(-L_K)$ in terms of concentric inner and outer ellipsoids and give improved bounds for origin-centred and origin-symmetric bodies. Combined with a weighted centroid identity for the polar body, these estimates yield an explicit $\varepsilon_n>0$ for which the unit ball is the only solution when $-n-\varepsilon_n\le p<-n$.
item.dc:creator: Yao Wan

item.title: Gradient estimates and Liouville properties for the drifted Laplacian
item.description: arXiv:2512.07389v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we discuss the validity of Liouville-type theorems involving the drifted Laplacian on complete, non-compact Riemannian manifolds endowed with a smooth vector field $X$. In particular, we prove new Liouville properties both for positive $X$-harmonic functions and for non-negative $X$-subharmonic functions which are in an $L^{p}$-space, $p\in(1,+\infty)$, with respect to any invariant measure for the operator. The main tool for the analysis is a local gradient estimate for positive solutions to the semilinear equation $\Delta_{X}u=F(u)$, which is valid if $F$ satisfies certain structural conditions and the Bakry-\'Emery-Ricci curvature associated to $X$ is bounded below. On the one hand, this estimate is used in a novel way to deduce the Liouville property for positive solutions and, on the other hand, it is used to construct cut-off functions for the $X$-Laplacian that yields the $L^{p}$-Liouville results.
item.dc:creator: Salvatore Lincastri

item.title: Heat kernel estimates for Markov processes with blowing-up jump kernels
item.description: arXiv:2512.24807v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we establish sharp two-sided heat kernel estimates for a large class of purely discontinuous symmetric Markov processes on closed subsets $F$ of $\mathbb{R}^d$, whose jump kernels blow up on a Borel subset $\Sigma$ of $F$. We assume that $F\setminus \Sigma$ is a $\kappa$-fat set and is dense in $F$, and additionally, in case of unbounded $F$, that the Assouad dimension of $F$ is strictly less than $d$. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work establishing sharp two-sided heat kernel estimates for jump processes whose jump kernels blow up on part of the state space. The jump kernels under consideration take the form $J(x,y)=|x-y|^{-d-\alpha}{\mathcal B}(x,y)$, where $\alpha\in (0,2)$ and the function ${\mathcal B}(x,y)$ blows up at a subset $\Sigma$ of $F$. A fundamental obstacle is that the tails of the jump measures are not uniformly bounded, and hence standard techniques in heat kernel analysis do not provide a priori off-diagonal estimates. To overcome this difficulty, we develop a new approach based on weighted integral estimates for the heat kernel that are sensitive to both the blow-up behavior of the jump kernel and the geometry of $F\setminus \Sigma$. Examples of processes falling within our general framework include traces of isotropic $\alpha$-stable processes in some unbounded $C^{1,\rm Dini}$ sets, processes in Lipschitz sets arising in connection with the nonlocal Neumann problem, and a large class of resurrected self-similar processes in the closed upper half-space.
item.dc:creator: Soobin Cho, Panki Kim, Renming Song, Zoran Vondra\v{c}ek

item.title: Averaging Dynamics and Wong-Zakai approximations for a Fast-Slow Navier-Stokes System Driven by fractional Brownian Motion
item.description: arXiv:2602.08680v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study a Fast-Slow system of coupled two- and three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations in which the fast component is perturbed by an additive fractional Brownian noise with Hurst parameter $\H>\frac{1}{3}$. Using rough path theory, we establish subsequential convergence in law of the slow component, with limiting dynamics depending on the Hurst parameter and the noise scaling. For $\H<\frac12$, an averaging regime yields a deterministic Navier-Stokes equation with an additional It\^o-Stokes drift. Under a stronger noise scaling, corresponding to a Wong-Zakai approximation, and a centering condition on the quadratic fast dynamics, we obtain a Navier-Stokes equation driven by fractional transport noise. For $\H>\frac12$, the transport-noise limit holds in the Wong-Zakai regime without this centering condition, with integration understood in the Young sense.
item.dc:creator: Eliseo Luongo, Francesco Triggiano

item.title: Non-local SDEs, critical drifts and local blow-ups
item.description: arXiv:2606.02786v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The paper is concerned with $\alpha$-stable SDEs with singular time-inhomogeneous general drift. Our drifts satisfy e.g.\,a close to minimal possible critical Morrey class condition that covers local blow-ups of the type arising in some particle systems with strong attracting interactions. We develop detailed Sobolev regularity theory for the forward and backward equations, construct Feller propagator and prove weak existence and conditional uniqueness for the $\alpha$-stable SDE.
item.dc:creator: Damir Kinzebulatov, Chengjun Yue

item.title: Finite-Time Singularities of Lagrangian Mean Curvature Flow with Quantitatively Precise Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2607.03152v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For each integer $K\geq2$ when $n\geq4$, and for $K=2,3,4$ when $n=3$, we construct an almost-calibrated Lagrangian mean curvature flow $L_K(t)$ in $\mathbb{C}^{n}$, starting from initial data arbitrarily close to being special Lagrangian, which develops a finite-time Type II singularity at time $T$ with the explicit curvature blow up rate \[ \sup_{L_{K}(t)} |\mathbf{A}_{L_{K}(t)}| \sim (T-t)^{-K/2} \qquad \text{as } t\nearrow T . \] The tangent flow at the singularity is a transverse pair of cohomogeneity-one special Lagrangian cones, while the Type II blow-up limit is a smooth cohomogeneity-one special Lagrangian desingularization. This gives a quantitative construction of Type II blow-up for a fully nonlinear parabolic PDE arising from cohomogeneity-one Lagrangian mean curvature flow. Our construction is based on a modulation analysis around a shrinking family of cohomogeneity-one special Lagrangian desingularizations, using the perturbative spectral theory developed in the companion paper.
item.dc:creator: Maxwell Stolarski, Wei-Bo Su

item.title: Logarithmic derivatives of variational and singular stochastic partial differential equations
item.description: arXiv:2608.21805v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a stochastic partial differential equation posed on a Gelfand triple and satisfying the fully local monotone conditions of R\"ockner, Shang and Zhang, we compute the logarithmic derivative of the law of the solution at a fixed time along a prescribed direction of the state space. The formula is intrinsic, expressed through the Hilbert-Schmidt Malliavin derivative $\Phi_r = \mathcal{D}_r X(t)$ and the covariance $\gamma_t = \int_0^t \Phi_r \Phi_r^{*}\,\mathrm{d}r$ alone, so that neither the inversion of the first variation nor uniform Malliavin-Sobolev bounds on the Tikhonov family are needed. It follows from an integration-by-parts identity on a Hilbert space, a Moore-Penrose covering field on Wiener space and a trace formula for the Tikhonov limit, brought to the equation by the representation $\Phi_r = Y(t,r)\mathcal{B}(r,X(r))$. The linearised theory is carried by $\Phi$ and by its own Malliavin derivative $\mathcal{W} = \mathcal{D}\Phi$, whose regularity is measured in the time-integrated quadratic energy that the dissipative structure of the linearisation produces, so that no operator norm of the first variation between the spaces of the triple occurs. The stochastic $p$-Laplacian and the two-dimensional Navier-Stokes equation are treated in detail; for the latter the dissipative, forcing and exponential-moment hypotheses are established together under trace-class additive noise and a smallness threshold on the noise covariance. A scalar reduction carries the identity beyond the variational class, to the law of a pairing $\langle u(t), \varphi\rangle$ for the singular equations of Bruned, Chandra, Chevyrev and Hairer, on the same H\"older triangle of moment exponents.
item.dc:creator: Ehsan Mirafzali, Frank Proske, Razvan Marinescu

item.title: The stable Bernstein theorem in $\mathbb{R}^{7}$
item.description: arXiv:2609.15720v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give a Green-function proof of the stable Bernstein theorem in $\mathbb R^7$ for smooth, connected, complete, two-sided stable minimal hypersurfaces, thus resolving the last case of the stable Bernstein problem.
item.dc:creator: Han Hong, Haizhong Li, Gaoming Wang

item.title: Pitt Inequalities and Logarithmic-type Uncertainty Principles for Metaplectic Operators
item.description: arXiv:2609.34946v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work, we provide a complete characterisation of Pitt's inequality for metaplectic operators. The symplectic geometry underlying a metaplectic operator distinguishes effective directions, along which its action is Fourier-type, from singular directions, along which concentration is preserved. For this reason, we adopt two complementary perspectives, thereby obtaining both an isotropic Pitt's inequality, emulating the classical theorem of Pitt, and an anisotropic inequality that adapts to the geometric features of the metaplectic group. As a by-product, we obtain Pitt's inequality for Fourier transforms along subspaces of $\rd$ and new quantitative time-dependent boundedness results for metaplectic operators on homogeneous Sobolev spaces, with applications to Schr\"odinger evolutions generated by quadratic Hamiltonians. Additionally, we derive logarithmic and entropic uncertainty principles for the metaplectic group. We show that the classical entropic uncertainty principle fails when both the effective and singular directions are present. In this case, a generally unbounded corrective entropy term accounts for the concentration-preserving directions and restores a meaningful lower bound. For quadratic Schr\"odinger evolutions, this correction follows the time-dependent geometry of the nondispersive directions and adjusts the uncertainty estimate accordingly.
item.dc:creator: Gianluca Giacchi, Itamar Oliveira, Amy Tierney

item.title: Gamma-Convergence of Weak-Type Nonlocal Functionals
item.description: arXiv:2610.07001v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $p\in[1,\infty)$, and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^N$ be a bounded open interval when $N=1$ or a bounded Lipschitz domain when $N\ge2$. For $\gamma\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$ and $\lambda\in(0,\infty)$, consider the weak-type nonlocal functional \begin{align*} F_{\lambda,p,\gamma}(u;\Omega):=\lambda^p \underset{\scriptscriptstyle |u(x)-u(y)|>\lambda|x-y|^{1+\gamma/p}} {\int_\Omega\int_\Omega}|x-y|^{\gamma-N}\,dy\,dx \end{align*} with $u:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$ measurable. We prove that, as $\lambda\to\infty$ for $\gamma\in(0,\infty)$ or as $\lambda\to0^+$ for $\gamma\in(-\infty,-1]$, $F_{\lambda,p,\gamma}(\cdot;\Omega)$ converges, in the sense of $\Gamma$-convergence in $L^p(\Omega)$, to \begin{align*} \Psi_{p,\gamma}^{\Omega}(u) :=\begin{cases} C_{N,p,\gamma}^{\rm cell}\displaystyle\int_\Omega|\nabla u|^p\,dx, &p\in(1,\infty)\ \hbox{and}\ u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega),\\ C_{N,1,\gamma}^{\rm cell}|Du|(\Omega), &p=1\ \hbox{and}\ u\in BV(\Omega),\\ \infty,&\hbox{otherwise}, \end{cases} \end{align*} where the positive constants $C_{N,p,\gamma}^{\mathrm{cell}}$ are independent of $\Omega$. We also establish the $\Gamma$-convergence of $F_{\lambda,p,\gamma}(\cdot;\mathbb R^N)$ in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^N)$ for all $\gamma\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$, with the limit functional having an additional term when $(N,p,\gamma)=(1,1,-1)$. These results affirmatively answer [Open Problem~9.3, Rend. Lincei Mat. Appl. 2023] of Brezis and also the other problem by Brezis et al. in [Section~7C, Anal. PDE 2024].
item.dc:creator: Xiaosheng Lin, Dachun Yang, Sibei Yang, Wen Yuan, Yangyang Zhang

item.title: The anisotropic Weyl law and Grassmannian equidistribution
item.description: arXiv:2610.18599v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish a Weyl law for the codimension-one anisotropic volume spectrum on compact Riemannian manifolds. We then use this law to obtain equidistribution in the full Grassmannian bundle while keeping the ambient metric fixed. More precisely, on every closed connected smooth Riemannian manifold of dimension three through six, we construct smooth, embedded hypersurfaces stationary for anisotropies smoothly converging to area. The cumulative sum of their area measures, when lifted to the Grassmannian bundle, converges to the uniform measure.
item.dc:creator: Antonio De Rosa, Aria Halavati

item.title: Emulating the Darcy Solution Operator by Heat-Semigroup Functional Calculus and Pointwise Products
item.description:
arXiv:2610.20106v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We approximate the Darcy solution operator $(a,f)\mapsto u$, where $-\operatorname{div}(a
abla u)=f$, by operator networks built only from heat-semigroup evaluations $e^{-tL_0}$ of a single fixed reference operator and pointwise products. The key obstacle is the variable-coefficient coupling $
abla a\cdot
abla u$. We show that it is produced by the heat product defect $[P_t(bu)-P_tb\,P_tu]/(2t)$, which converges quantitatively to $
abla b\cdot
abla u$. Inserted into a Laplacian-preconditioned Richardson iteration, this yields an explicit scheme of depth $O(\log(1/\varepsilon)/\log(1/q))$ whose $\dot H^1$ error is at most $\varepsilon$, uniformly over the coefficient class and $L^2$ data, with all parameters explicit. Each block is controlled in continuum operator norm, without Galerkin truncation. On the torus, band-limited inputs admit an exact pseudo-spectral realization on a grid of $O(1/(\varepsilon a_{\min}))$ points per direction, up to logarithmic and class-dependent factors. The argument extends by carre du champ calculus to strongly local Dirichlet spaces with a spectral gap and a Bakry--Emery bound $\mathrm{BE}(-K,\infty)$, with dimension-independent constants after spectral-gap normalization. On the torus we also obtain a $C^2$-type coefficient class and a refinement to Wiener classes of regularity $1+	heta$, with product-defect rate $t^{	heta/2}$. The factor $1/(2t)$ makes the proved scheme ill-conditioned at small $\varepsilon$.
